PROPOSED RESOLUTION

GREATER CHICAGOLAND ECONOMIC PARTNERSHIP UPDATE 

WHEREAS, the Greater Chicagoland Economic Partnership (GCEP) is an economic development initiative for the seven-county region of northeastern Illinois (the "Region") created by the economic development organizations and elected officials of the Region to partner and collaborate on specific projects, share resources, and provide data and analysis to improve and enhance economic development within the Region; and

WHEREAS, the GCEP aims to strengthen the seven-county region’s resiliency and competitiveness by fostering opportunities for collaboration on initiatives that benefit the entire Region; and

WHEREAS, each of the seven counties and the City of Chicago via its agent, World Business Chicago, committed to the annual costs set forth in the Agreement which vary for each of the participating jurisdictions based on population and economic output; and

WHEREAS, the Cook County Board approved Resolution 25-3921 on 10/23/2025, authorizing the Cook County Bureau of Economic Development to enter into an agreement and fulfill its annual financial contribution to support continuation of the Greater Chicagoland Economic Partnership in 2026; and 

WHEREAS, Resolution 25-3921 stated that Cook County will request that World Business Chicago (WBC) report to the Cook County Board in 2026 to review its work to date and outline plans for the coming year, and 

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners requests the Bureau of Economic Development arrange for World Business Chicago to provide a review of its work related to the Greater Chicagoland Economic Partnership to the Cook County Business and Economic Development Committee

il-17031-bos-matter-80643.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

CONGRATULATING THE COOK COUNTY CLERK’S OFFICE ON RECEIVING THE U.S. ELECTION ASSISTANCE COMMISSION’S CLEARINGHOUSE AWARD FOR EXCELLENCE IN ELECTION ADMINISTRATION

WHEREAS, as the chief election authority for suburban Cook County, the Cook County Clerk bears the vital responsibility of safeguarding elections that are fair, efficient, accessible, and secure, a charge that Cook County Clerk Monica Gordon has embraced with seriousness, integrity, and a steadfast commitment to expanding voter participation; and

WHEREAS, recognizing the importance of investing in the next generation of civic leaders, Clerk Monica Gordon launched a High School Early Voting Program for the 2026 Gubernatorial Election in Cook County, placing students at the center of real-world election operations as both Election Judges and voters; and

WHEREAS, the Clerk’s “Defenders of DA’mocracy” program is believed to be the first of its kind in the nation and was developed through a public-private partnership with the Chicago Bears; and through Bears-branded materials, video messages, and leadership participation, the initiative uses a culturally relevant platform to engage students in meaningful civic participation and make the election process tangible and exciting for young people; and

WHEREAS, students from 24 suburban high schools were trained and certified as official Election Judges to operate on-campus Early Voting sites for the March 17 Gubernatorial Primary, and, under the supervision of the Clerk’s Office, they managed voter check-in, ballot processing, and equipment while adhering to strict security and chain-of-custody protocols, thereby gaining an authentic and hands-on civic experience; and

WHEREAS, the initiative builds civic confidence, demystifies election administration, and cultivates a pipeline of future Election Judges and engaged young voters; and with the support of the Chicago Bears amplifying outreach, the program demonstrates how innovative partnerships can expand participation and empower the next generation of civic leaders; and

WHEREAS, by combining traditional election tools, including voter check-in systems and ballot processing, with innovative engagement strategies, the program cultivates future civic leaders while expanding participation; and its adaptable design offers a scalable model that can be replicated to engage young people in meaningful, hands-on civic participation; and

WHEREAS, the program strengthens outcomes for voters, students, and election administrators alike; and by placing Early Voting sites inside high schools, it removes barriers and provides convenient, trusted locations within local communities, while introducing young voters to the process in a familiar environment that increases confidence and encourages long-term participation; and

WHEREAS, the program builds a sustainable pipeline of trained Election Judges and Polling Place Technicians; and students receive hands-on training, gain paid civic experience, and often return to serve in future elections, an investment that reduces staffing shortages, enhances professionalism at polling locations, and strengthens operational continuity; and beyond its operational value, the initiative has instilled a renewed sense of pride among Elections staff, who play a direct role in welcoming young voters into a lifelong relationship with civic participation; and

WHEREAS, the program transforms civic education into civic action, cultivating the next generation of informed voters and defenders of democracy while strengthening election operations for years to come; and

WHEREAS, this year, the Cook County Clerk’s Office was recognized by the U.S. Election Assistance Commission (EAC) with a national Clearinghouse Award for excellence in election administration in the category of Distinguished Voter Education and Communications Initiatives for its innovative High School Early Voting Program; and

WHEREAS, the EAC presents these awards annually to recognize best practices in election administration, and the Clerk’s Defenders of DA’mocracy High School Early Voting Program was one of 46 programs nationwide to receive a Clearinghouse Award; and

WHEREAS, also known as the “Clearies,” these awards play an essential role in fulfilling the EAC’s mission under the Help America Vote Act to serve as a clearinghouse for election administration information, and the EAC is an independent, bipartisan federal agency solely focused on election administration; and

WHEREAS, the Cook County Clerk’s Office will continue expanding the Defenders of DA’mocracy initiative by creating new opportunities for young people to engage with leadership, government, and civic participation in ways that feel real and meaningful, including bringing interactive civic engagement experiences directly into classrooms across the county and offering Civics and Social Sciences instruction focused on voting, elections, leadership, civic responsibility, and community impact.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, by the President and members of the Cook County Board of Commissioners that this body hereby congratulates Cook County Clerk Monica Gordon and the Cook County Clerk’s Office on receiving the EAC’s Clearinghouse Award for the Defenders of DA’mocracy High School Early Voting Program; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Board of Commissioners commends and supports continued efforts to expand this program and encourages broader participation in its events and initiatives so that more young people may serve as Election Judges and become meaningfully engaged in the electoral process.

Chicago Industrial LL, LLC 6B PROPERTY TAX INCENTIVE REQUEST 

WHEREAS, the Cook County Bureau of Economic Development received and reviewed a Real Property Assessment Classification 6b application containing the following information: 

Applicant: Chicago Industrial LL, LLC

Address: 350 Howard Ave, Des Plaines, Illinois 60018 

Municipality or Unincorporated Township: Village of Des Plaines 

Cook County District: 17th District 

Permanent Index Number: 09-30-101-029-0000

Municipal Resolution Number: Village of Des Plaines Resolution #49-26 

Number of month property vacant/abandoned: 28 months vacant 

Special circumstances justification requested: Yes or No 

Proposed use of property:  Industrial use - warehousing, manufacturing  and distribution  

Living Wage Ordinance Compliance Affidavit Provided: Yes   

WHEREAS, the Cook County Board of Commissioners has adopted a Real Property Assessment Classification 6b that provides an applicant a reduction in the assessment level for an abandoned industrial facility; and

WHEREAS, the Cook County Classification System for Assessment defines abandoned property as buildings and other structures that, after having been vacant and unused for at least 12 continuous months, there has been no purchased for value by a purchaser and the property is in need of substantial rehabilitation ; and

WHEREAS, in the instance where the property does not meet the definition of abandoned property, the municipality or the Board of Commissioners, may determine that special circumstances may exist that justify finding that the property is abandoned for purpose of Class 6b; and

WHEREAS, in the case of abandonment of at least 12 months and no purchase for value by a disinterested buyer, the County may determine that special circumstances justify finding the property as being deemed abandoned; and

WHEREAS, Class 6b requires a resolution by the County Board validating the property as abandoned for the purpose of Class 6b; and

WHEREAS, the municipality states the Class 6b is necessary for development to occur on this specific real estate. The municipal resolution cites the qualifications of this property to meet the definition of abandoned with special circumstances; and

WHEREAS; industrial real estate is normally assessed at 25% of its market value, qualifying industrial real estate eligible for the Class 6b can receive a significant reduction in the level of assessment from the date that new construction or rehabilitation has been completed, or in the case of abandoned property from the date of substantial re-occupancy.   Properties receiving Class 6b will be assessed at 10% of the market value for 10 years, 15% for the 11th year and 20% in the 12th year; and  

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, by the President and Board of Commissioners of the County of Cook, that the President and Board of Commissioners validate the above-captioned property is deemed abandoned with special circumstances under the Class 6b; and 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the County Clerk is hereby authorized and directed to forward a certified copy of this resolution to the Office of the Cook County Assessor

il-17031-bos-matter-80826.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

CHICAGO-COOK COUNTY TASK FORCE TO REDUCE VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN RECOMMENDATIONS REPORTING REQUIREMENT

WHEREAS, the Cook County Board of Commissioners took a stance to work towards the full protection of domestic violence and gender-based violence survivors; and

WHEREAS, as part of the Cook County Domestic Violence Initiative, the Board passed an amendment to provide funding as part of the FY2022 budget to improve and expand services for survivors of domestic violence, to address the immediate needs of Domestic Violence Court operations and to establish a 24-hour, 7 day a week court operation for Domestic Violence Court proceedings; and

WHEREAS, said measure was to ensure that adequate funding is available to improve and streamline operations, increase efficiency, and provide accurate information in the criminal justice system, all with the goal of ensuring the public safety of the residents of Cook County; and

WHEREAS, the processes in the criminal justice system are important to the day-to-day operations and are heavily relied on for the safety of victim-witnesses; and

WHEREAS, in addition to domestic violence processes, domestic relations especially when a child is involved are also key in ensuring both victims and the welfare of children are protected; and

WHEREAS, in 2023, the Board of Commissioners called for a public hearing and these matter and again in 2025, to hear from advocates and county public safety stakeholders on the implementation of safeguards for the protection of gender-based violence survivors and domestic
relations mediations and child representation; and

WHEREAS, due to the exponential increase in domestic violence, and as a result of such hearing, Cook County and the City of Chicago created the Chicago-Cook County Task Force to Reduce Violence Against Women to make recommendations to the Mayor of the City of Chicago, the Chicago City Council, the President of the Cook County Board of Commissioners, and the Cook County Board of Commissioners concerning the formulation of a comprehensive strategy to collaboratively address violence against women in the City of Chicago and the County of Cook; and

WHEREAS, the task force endeavored to initiate a whole-government approach; incorporate the findings of previous and concurrent task forces relating to women and vulnerable communities; and focus on governmental responsibility to address violence against women; and

WHEREAS, the final independent report of the Task Force was presented in July 2026, providing recommendations on identified gaps, including data-sharing, oversight, and policy recommendations for future collaborative actions; and

WHEREAS, the report outlined a comprehensive list of recommendations aimed at enhancing the measures employed to address domestic violence-related issues and to support victims; and

WHEREAS, to ensure the implementation of the report’s recommendations, for the City of Chicago and Cook County governments, it is important to commit to reporting progress to both governmental bodies on a regular basis;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners hereby requests that the Criminal Justice Stakeholders provide a comprehensive outline of necessary measures needed to implement the recommendations of the Final Report of the Chicago-Cook County Task Force to Reduce Violence Against Women; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that a quarterly meeting of the Criminal Justice Committee of the Board of Commissioners shall be convened to receive an update on the progress being made towards achieving the aforementioned recommendations, commencing with the 1st quarter of the 2027 fiscal year.


Effective Date: This Resolution shall be effective upon passage.

il-17031-bos-matter-80854.title:
PROPOSED ORDINANCE AMENDMENT

VITAL RECORDS FEES FOR COUNTY CLERK

BE IT ORDAINED, By The Cook County Board Of Commissioners, That Chapter 2 Administration, Article IV Officers and Employees, Subdivision II. Fees, Section 2-174 Vital records fees for County Clerk of the Cook County Code is hereby amended as Follows:

Sec. 2-174.  Vital records fees for County Clerk.

(a)	Birth records. The Cook County Clerk shall continue to charge and collect a fee for the first copy, and a fee for each additional copy of a birth record as set out in Section 32-1. The following individuals may receive a copy of their birth record at no cost. 

(1)	Individuals, or not for profit organizations representing such individuals, who meet the definition of homeless as defined by Section 103 the federal McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act of 1987, (42 U.S.C. 11302, et seq.), or any individual residing in any of the living situations defined in 42 U.S.C. 11434a(2), as such statutes existed at the time of the enactment of this ordinance; or.

(2)	Individuals in the custody of, or who have been released within the previous 90 days by, the Cook County Department of Corrections or the Illinois Department of Corrections; or

(3)	Individuals residing in a shelter for victims of domestic violence. who are the victims of domestic, sexual, or gender violence, and their dependents, and who provide documentation from the entity where the individual has sought assistance in addressing domestic violence, sexual violence, or gender violence. The documentation may come from an employee, agent or volunteer of any victim services organization, such as a shelter or non-profit organization, an attorney or legal aid organization, a member of the clergy, or a medical provider. Documentation may also include an official police report or court order. Documents must be dated within the last 12 months. 

The Cook County Clerk may promulgate regulations to determine how individuals can apply for a no cost birth record. 

(b)	Marriage records. The Cook County Clerk shall charge and collect a fee for the issuance of a marriage license, sealing, filing and recording the same and the certificate thereunto as set out in Section 32-1. The Cook County Clerk shall continue to charge and collect a fee for the first copy, and a fee for each additional copy of a marriage record as set out in Section 32-1. 

(c)	Death records. The Cook County Clerk shall charge and collect a fee for the first copy, and a fee for each additional copy of a death record as set out in Section 32-1. 

(d)	Genealogical records. The County Clerk shall charge and collect a fee as set out in Section 32-1 for the first copy and a fee as set out in Section 32-1 for subsequent copies of any genealogical birth, death or marriage certificate. 

(e)	Emergency fee. The County Clerk shall charge and collect an emergency fee as set out in Section 32-1 for providing a copy of a vital record on an overnight basis. The emergency fee authorized in this subsection shall be in addition to any other fees authorized to be collected by the County Clerk for providing the requested document. 

(f)	Waiver and refund of death record fee. The County Clerk shall waive the County portion of the vital records fee for death records requested (first copy only) as set forth in Section 32-1 by those persons legally authorized to request and obtain a death certificate and seeking a copy of a death certificate for a decedent buried at Burr Oak Cemetery. Said waiver shall apply only to death records indicating a date of death prior to July 6, 2009, and burial at Burr Oak Cemetery; the waiver extends only to the County's portion of the fee for the first copy only and shall not extend to requests for additional copies. The County Clerk is required to continue to collect a $2.00 fee for the first copy of the death record as required by State Statute unless waived by the State. The waiver shall run through September 15, 2009, unless otherwise authorized by the Cook County Board of Commissioners. In accordance with the County Clerk's records, the County Clerk is hereby authorized to refund Cook County's portion of the death records fee for death records requested (first copy only) to those individuals who legally requested and obtained a death record/certificate since July 6, 2009, for a decedent buried at Burr Oak Cemetery. 

(g)	Civil Union records. The Cook County Clerk shall charge and collect a fee for the issuance of a civil union license, sealing, filing and recording the same and the certificate thereunto as set out in Section 32-1. The Cook County Clerk shall charge and collect a fee for the first copy, and a fee for each additional copy of a civil union record as set out in Section 32-1. 

(h)	Commemorative Certificates. The Cook County Clerk shall charge and collect a fee for the issuance of a Commemorative Certificate of Marriage or for the issuance of a Commemorative Certificate of Civil Union as set out in Section 32-1. With each Commemorative Certificate issued, the Clerk shall also issue a certified copy of the underlying record. The fee charged and collected as set forth in Section 32-1 shall cover the cost of both the commemorative certificate and the certified copy.

Effective date:  This ordinance shall be in effect immediately upon adoption.

il-17031-bos-matter-80873.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

RESOLUTION EXPRESSING SUPPORT FOR AN INDEPENDENT REVIEW OF THE COOK COUNTY JAIL

WHEREAS, the Cook County Board of Commissioners is committed to improving public health and safety and has invested substantial resources to further that goal, including substance use disorder treatment, harm reduction programs, community-based violence intervention initiatives, and policies and programs aimed at increasing pretrial fairness; and

WHEREAS, the Cook County Department of Corrections is one of the largest single-site jails in the country, expanding ninety-six acres and eight city blocks, and as of February 2026, averages a population of around 6,000 individuals in custody; and

WHEREAS, according to multiple reports from sources such as the Vera Institute for Justice, the Cook County Jail is one of the largest institutions that jails people with mental health needs; and 

WHEREAS, Cermak Health Services is the accredited provider of health services to individuals in custody at the Cook County Jail, and provides primary care, specialty care, oral health, mental health, rehabilitative and infirmary-level care to its patients; and

WHEREAS, the Cook County Sheriff and Cermak Health Services have legal and medical responsibilities to ensure the safety and well-being of individuals in custody; and

WHEREAS, between 2020 and 2025, 61 people have died while in the custody of the Cook County jail, with the most deaths occurring in 2023; and

WHEREAS, these deaths were the subject of a hearing before the Criminal Justice Committee on December 18, 2024; and

WHEREAS, while the Cook County Jail does not currently have an independent and external body reporting on the conditions of the jail, independent monitors have been shown to be a critical tool for identifying systemic failures, increasing transparency, and implementing reforms to improve conditions and services within such facilities; and

WHEREAS, the Cook County Jail was previously monitored by the John Howard Association from 1982 until 2011 and regularly provided reports on jail conditions.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, the Cook County Board of Commissioners is committed to the wellbeing of individuals detained in the Cook County Jail; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners expresses support for an independent review of the Cook County Jail by an independent and external organization, focusing on the health, safety and wellness of the detainees and conditions of confinement; and 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that copies of this resolution be delivered to the Cook County Sheriff, Cook County Health Cermak Health Services, Justice Advisory Council, Law Office of the Cook County Public defender, Office of the Chief Judge of the Circuit Court of Cook County, Cook County State’s Attorney’s Office, Cook County Department of Public Health, and all other appropriate County agencies, bureaus and offices. ..end

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, by the President and Board of Commissioners of the County of Cook, that the President and Board of Commissioners validate the above-captioned property is deemed abandoned with special circumstances under the Class 8; and 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the County Clerk is hereby authorized and directed to forward a certified copy of this resolution to the Office of the Cook County Assessor.

Address: 4011 Lincoln Highway, Matteson, Illinois 

Municipality or Unincorporated Township: Village of Matteson 

Cook County District: 6th District 

Permanent Index Number: 31-22-401-018-0000 

Municipal Resolution Number: Village of Matteson Resolution Number 1398-0425 

Number of month property vacant/abandoned: 38 months vacant 

Special circumstances justification requested: Yes 

Proposed use of property:  Commercial use -  fitness gym 

Living Wage Ordinance Compliance Affidavit Provided: No  

WHEREAS, the Cook County Board of Commissioners has adopted a Real Property Assessment Classification 8 that provides an applicant a reduction in the assessment level for an abandoned commercial facility; and

WHEREAS, the Cook County Classification System for Assessment defines abandoned property as buildings and other structures that, after having been vacant and unused for at least 12 continuous months, have been purchased for value by a purchaser in whom the seller has no direct financial interest; and

WHEREAS, in the instance where the property does not meet the definition of abandoned property, the municipality or the Board of Commissioners, may determine that special circumstances may exist that justify finding that the property is abandoned for purpose of Class 8; and

WHEREAS, in the case of abandonment of less than 12 months and purchase for value, by a purchaser in whom the seller has no direct financial interest, the County may determine that special circumstances justify finding the property is deemed abandoned; and

WHEREAS, Class 8 requires the validation by the County Board of the shortened period of qualifying abandonment in cases where the facility has been abandoned for less than 12 consecutive months upon purchase for value; and

WHEREAS, the municipality states the Class 8 is necessary for development to occur on this specific real estate. The municipal resolution cites the qualifications of this property to meet the definition of abandoned with special circumstances; and

WHEREAS; commercial real estate is normally assessed at 25% of its market value, qualifying commercial real estate eligible for the Class 8 can receive a significant reduction in the level of assessment from the date that new construction or rehabilitation has been completed, or in the case of abandoned property from the date of substantial re-occupancy.   Properties receiving Class 8 will be assessed at 10% of the market value for 10 years, 15% for the 11th year and 20% in the 12th year; and  

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, by the President and Board of Commissioners of the County of Cook, that the President and Board of Commissioners validate the above-captioned property is deemed abandoned with special circumstances under the Class 8; and 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the County Clerk is hereby authorized and directed to forward a certified copy of this resolution to the Office of the Cook County Assessor

il-17031-bos-matter-80941.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

A RESOLUTION HONORING THE LIFE, LEGACY, AND EXTRAORDINARY SERVICE OF PASTOR DAVID COLEMAN, SR.

WHEREAS, Pastor David Coleman, Sr. devoted his life to faith, family, public service, and the advancement of Chicago's Englewood community, leaving an enduring legacy of compassion, leadership, and unwavering commitment to others; and

WHEREAS, Pastor David Coleman, Sr. was born on May 14, 1934, in Parkdale, Arkansas, the seventh of eleven children born to Reverend John and Ruby Coleman. Raised in a household rooted in faith, hard work, perseverance, and service, he carried these values throughout every aspect of his life and ministry; and

WHEREAS, following the passing of his father, Reverend John Coleman, in 1967, Pastor David Coleman, Sr. accepted the call to serve as Pastor of New Mt. Sinai Missionary Baptist Church. For more than five decades, until his retirement in 2020, he faithfully led the congregation, providing steadfast spiritual guidance while transforming the church into a cornerstone of hope, fellowship, and service for countless families throughout Chicago's South Side; and

WHEREAS, Pastor Coleman believed that ministry extended beyond the pulpit. A gifted craftsman and self-taught master repairman, he personally purchased, renovated, and transformed a former warehouse located at 1235 West 59th Street into the permanent home of New Mt. Sinai Missionary Baptist Church. Through his own labor and vision, he created not only a sanctuary for worship but also a welcoming community center where youth ministries, choir programs, neighborhood meetings, food distributions, educational activities, and countless community events strengthened the fabric of Englewood; and

WHEREAS, Pastor Coleman further demonstrated his servant leadership through more than twenty years of dedicated service as the maintenance supervisor at Stone Terrace Apartments, where he became widely respected for his craftsmanship, integrity, and willingness to help others. Whether repairing buildings, solving maintenance challenges, or assisting residents in need, he viewed every task as an extension of his ministry, believing that serving people with his hands was equally as important as serving them through his faith; and

WHEREAS, Pastor Coleman's church became a significant center for civic engagement and community empowerment. The sanctuary at New Mt. Sinai Missionary Baptist Church served as an important gathering place for neighborhood organizing and hosted early campaign activities during the historic mayoral campaign of the late Mayor Harold Washington, reflecting Pastor Coleman's enduring belief that faith communities should actively participate in strengthening democracy and advocating for their neighborhoods; and

WHEREAS, Pastor Coleman's commitment to service inspired generations within his own family. His legacy continues through his children and grandchildren, including his youngest daughter, Alderman Stephanie D. Coleman of Chicago's 16th Ward, whose distinguished public service reflects the values of integrity, compassion, faith, and community stewardship instilled by her father; and

WHEREAS, throughout his remarkable life, Pastor David Coleman, Sr. exemplified humility, selflessness, and unwavering dedication. Whether preaching the Gospel, rebuilding a church with his own hands, mentoring young people, repairing homes and buildings, opening the church to neighbors in need, or quietly serving his community through acts of kindness, he demonstrated that true leadership is measured not by titles, but by service to others; and

WHEREAS, Pastor David Coleman, Sr.'s extraordinary contributions to the spiritual, civic, and social life of Chicago's Englewood community have left an indelible mark upon Chicago and Cook County and will continue to inspire future generations to live lives grounded in faith, compassion, service, and love for their communities;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the President and Members of the Cook County Board of Commissioners do hereby honor the life, legacy, and extraordinary service of Pastor David Coleman, Sr., recognize his immeasurable contributions to the people of Cook County, and express their deepest gratitude for his decades of faithful leadership, community service, and unwavering commitment to improving the lives of others; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that a suitable copy of this Resolution be presented to the family of Pastor David Coleman, Sr. as a lasting expression of the respect and appreciation of the President and Members of the Cook County Board of Commissioners, and as a tribute to a life well lived in faithful service to God, family, and community.

il-17031-bos-matter-80976.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

HONORING JENNIFER ‘SIS’ KILLEN UPON THE OCCASION OF HER DEPARTURE FROM SERVICE TO COOK COUNTY, ILLINOIS  

WHEREAS, Jennifer ‘Sis’ Killen has had an accomplished and widely admired 27-year career in the transportation industry; and

WHEREAS, Sis began her tenure with Cook County in 2012 as Bureau Chief for the Department of Transportation and Highways (DoTH) Transportation and Planning section, where she oversaw the traffic, project studies, programming, agreements and right-of-way divisions; and 

WHEREAS, in 2013, she was promoted to DoTH Assistant Superintendent - the first female to achieve the title - where she assisted the Superintendent with all department functions, and oversaw six bureaus that perform planning, design, construction, maintenance and administrative activities; and  

WHEREAS, in April 2021, Sis was appointed as Superintendent of DoTH, again making County history as the first female to hold the title in the department’s 113-year history, where she was charged with the planning, design, operation, maintenance and construction of 561 centerline miles of roadway and 1,620 lane miles of pavement; and 

WHEREAS, Sis is currently leading the department’s largest ever capital program, including the advancement of projects of regional significance, and has positioned DoTH to provide the transportation leadership, expertise and resources required to advance such projects that involve multiple agency and municipal boundaries; and

WHEREAS, Sis co-led the completion of the County’s first long-range transportation plan in 75 years, a transformative initiative that promoted a multimodal policy framework to guide investments, equitable access to and modernization of transportation and brought countless benefits to the people of Cook County; and 

WHEREAS, she has been a key orchestrator in transforming the department from a road-centric agency to an organization that prioritizes transit, bicycle and pedestrian traffic; and

WHEREAS, since Sis joined the County, she has been recognized by multiple organizations for her exceptional contributions; and 

WHEREAS, in 2019, Sis was honored as ‘Woman of the Year’ by the Women’s Transportation Seminar Chicago Chapter in recognition of her outstanding contribution to the transportation industry and advancing women and minorities within the field; and 

WHEREAS, in 2021, Sis was awarded the March of Dimes Leadership in the Public Sector Award in recognition of advancing critical public works, transit improvements and community development projects in the region; and

WHEREAS, in 2024, Sis was awarded Government Civil Engineer of the Year by the Illinois Section of the American Society of Civil Engineers in recognition of her significant, lasting contributions to public service and the engineering profession; and

WHEREAS, Sis will be departing as Superintendent of DoTH on September 24, 2026; and 

WHEREAS, She spent 13 years in private consulting providing engineering services to municipal clients before joining the County; and 

WHEREAS, Sis began her career through a cooperative education internship at Chicago Area Transportation Study, now known as Chicago Metropolitan Agency for Planning, where she served as chairwoman of the Transportation Committee from 2015 - 2018 during the development of the region’s ONTO 2050 planning update; and  

WHEREAS, Sis is a graduate of the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, earning her Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering in 1999, and she is also a 2019 graduate of the University of Chicago’s Civic Leadership Academy; and 

WHEREAS, Sis has consistently demonstrated professionalism, collaboration and a clear dedication to public service as a leader in design, collaboration, innovation and policy making, and truly understands the critical role equity plays in transportation investments that support community growth; and

WHEREAS, throughout her career with Cook County, Sis has shown not only a commitment to operational excellence, but also a deep knowledge of transportation systems that have strengthened the County’s ability to deliver safe and reliable mobility for residents; and

WHEREAS, having ably and dutifully served the residents of Cook County for 14 years, Cook County wishes Sis well in the next chapter of her life, with the support of her husband Kevin, sons Brendan and Charlie and daughter Bridget.

NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the President and members of the Board of Commissioners, on behalf of the 5.2 million residents and over 22,000 employees of Cook County, thank Sis for her dedication, service and her unwavering commitment to Cook County; and 

BE IT FURTHER RESOVLED, that a suitable copy of this Resolution be spread upon the official proceedings of this Honorable Body and that an official copy of the same be tendered to Sis Killen.

il-17031-bos-matter-80982.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

JAIME IRENE JONES, IN MEMORIAM

WHEREAS, Jamie Irene Jones (nee Humphrey) passed away peacefully on August 14th in her Woodridge home, surrounded by her family, after a 10-year journey with breast cancer; and

WHEREAS, Jamie Irene Jones was born in Chicago and grew up as one of three sisters. A 2000 graduate of Willowbrook High School, Jamie met David Jones in 1999, who would later become the love of her life. After being set up to attend a wedding in 2003-a date Jamie would fondly call her “Best Date Ever”-Jamie and Dave were married in 2007; and

WHEREAS, Jamie Irene Jones is survived by her beloved husband, David, and her children, Nicholas, Emma, Irena, and Michaela; and

WHEREAS, Jamie Irene Jones was the devoted sister of Michelle Bukowski and Beth Schneider; and

WHEREAS, Jamie Irene Jones faithfully served the people of Cook County Government for 20 years; and

WHEREAS, Jamie Irene Jones began working for the Cook County Highway Department as a summer aide, working and assisting in various divisions of the Department, including Personnel, the Map Division, the Design Bureau, the Permits Division, and the Office of the Superintendent of Highways; and

WHEREAS, Jamie Irene Jones began working full-time for the Cook County Superintendent of Highways in September 2000 and later assisted in the Design Bureau; and

WHEREAS, from 2003 through 2008, Jamie Irene Jones worked for the Cook County Department of Office Technology as an Administrative Assistant to the Director, while also working at the Technology Help Desk and serving as a timekeeper; and

WHEREAS, Jamie Irene Jones’ talents and dedication led to her move to the Office of the Secretary to the Board in 2008. Jamie Jones would become the face of the Secretary to the Board’s Office to members of the public, Commissioners, and staff; and

WHEREAS, Jamie Irene Jones faced numerous challenges throughout her battle with cancer; however, she remained determined to persevere with a positive attitude. Surrounded by the support of her family, physicians, and colleagues, she strived to live by the motto, “Make each day meaningful”; and

WHEREAS, Jamie Irene Jones leaves behind a legacy defined by her unwavering commitment to her family and community; and

WHEREAS, all who knew her will attest that Jamie Irene Jones was a kind and compassionate woman, virtuous in character and gentle in spirit, admired and respected by her many friends and neighbors, and dearly loved by her family; now, therefore,

BE IT RESOLVED, by the Board of Commissioners of Cook County, that the Board does hereby offer its deepest condolences and most heartfelt sympathy to the family and many friends of Jamie Irene Jones and joins them in sorrow; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that this text be spread upon the official proceedings of this Honorable Body, and that a suitable copy of the same be tendered to the family of Jamie Irene Jones, that her memory may be so honored and ever cherished.

.

il-17031-bos-matter-80988.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

APPOINTING AN ACTING COUNTY SUPERINTENDENT OF HIGHWAYS

WHEREAS, a vacancy will exist in the office of the Superintendent of Highways of Cook County, Illinois in the Department of Transportation and Highways on September 25, 2026 due to the resignation of the incumbent County Superintendent of Highways, Jennifer “Sis” Killen which will occur at the end of business day on September 24, 2026; and

WHEREAS, in accordance with Section 5-204 of the Illinois Highway Code, consent of the Illinois Department of Transportation (“IDOT”) shall be secured for the appointment of an Acting County Superintendent of Highways; and

Summary/Notes:  The Department of Emergency Management and Regional Security (EMRS) seeks authorization to enter into the Illinois Emergency Management Mutual Aid System (IEMMAS) Intergovernmental Service Agreement, a statewide mutual aid network that enables participating local governments to request and provide emergency management assistance during disasters and other emergency situations. Through the agreement, Cook County would be able to request personnel, equipment, materials and other emergency management resources from participating jurisdictions when an incident exceeds the County’s available capabilities. Likewise, when resources and operational conditions permit, EMRS could provide assistance to other participating jurisdictions experiencing an emergency.
Participation in IEMMAS would provide Cook County with an additional mechanism to supplement its emergency response capabilities and strengthen regional coordination during significant incidents. The agreement does not require a membership fee or other direct cost to participate, and participation in the Illinois Emergency Services Management Association (IESMA) is not a prerequisite. Requests for assistance are coordinated through the system’s 24-hour dispatch center, with resources provided by participating jurisdictions based on availability and operational needs. The agreement allows for termination for any reason with 90 days written notice.

il-17031-bos-matter-81014.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

HONORING SEPTEMBER 18, 2026 AS NATIONAL POW/MIA RECOGNITION DAY

WHEREAS, throughout our Nation’s history, American service members held as Prisoners of War have endured extraordinary sacrifice, including isolation, captivity, trauma, hardship and, in some cases, inhumane treatment in violation of international law and the standards of human dignity; and
 
WHEREAS, National POW/MIA Recognition Day was established in 1979 by proclamation of President Jimmy Carter and has since been observed annually on the third Friday of September to honor former Prisoners of War and those who remain missing and unaccounted for; and
 
WHEREAS, generations of American service members have answered our Nation’s call to duty, many risking capture, imprisonment, injury and death in defense of our country. On National POW/MIA Recognition Day, we honor those who endured captivity, remember those who remain missing and unaccounted for and stand with the families who continue to await answers; and
 
WHEREAS, nearly 81,000 Americans remain missing from past conflicts, and the continuing work to locate, identify and account for our Nation’s missing personnel represents an enduring commitment to their families and to the promise that their service and sacrifice will never be forgotten; and
 
WHEREAS, Cook County remains committed to honoring the service and sacrifice of our Nation’s veterans, active-duty service members, former Prisoners of War, those who remain missing or unaccounted for and the families who have carried the uncertainty of a loved one’s absence; and
 
WHEREAS, Cook County recognizes that the freedoms enjoyed by our communities were secured and preserved through the service and sacrifice of generations of Americans in uniform and that remembering our Prisoners of War and those Missing in Action is an obligation that extends beyond a single day of recognition; and 

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the President and the Cook County Board of Commissioners do hereby recognize September 18, 2026, as National POW/MIA Recognition Day in Cook County and encourage residents throughout Cook County to join in honoring former Prisoners of War, remembering those who remain missing and unaccounted for, supporting their families and reaffirming our enduring commitment that they will never be forgotten; and 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the President and the Cook County Board of Commissioners recognize and honor the service, sacrifice, courage and resilience of all former Prisoners of War and those who remain Missing in Action and reaffirm the enduring national commitment to account for and bring home America’s missing service members; and
 
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that this text be spread upon the official proceedings of this Honorable Body in recognition of National POW/MIA Recognition Day.

il-17031-bos-matter-81021.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

SUPPORTING THE MAJOR RICHARDSON STAR ACT 

WHEREAS, Cook County has a longstanding commitment to supporting veterans, service members and their families; and
 
WHEREAS, Major Richard Star served in Iraq and Afghanistan and was medically retired after developing lung cancer following exposure to burn pits during his military service; and
 
WHEREAS, under current federal law, certain combat-injured veterans who are medically retired before completing 20 years of service cannot receive the full amount of both their military retirement pay and Department of Veterans Affairs disability compensation; and 

WHEREAS, Cook County is home to approximately 137,000 veterans, including more than 32,000 veterans receiving service-connected disability compensation, and recognizes that federal policies affecting military retirement and disability benefits have a direct impact on veterans and military families throughout the County; and
 
WHEREAS, the Major Richard Star Act would address this issue by allowing eligible combat-injured, medically retired service members to receive both benefits without the current offset; and 

WHEREAS, the Illinois House of Representatives adopted House Resolution 722 in support of the Major Richard Star Act and urged Congress to act on this issue; and
 
WHEREAS, Cook County recognizes the service and sacrifice of combat-injured veterans and the importance of ensuring they receive the benefits earned through their military service; and
 
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the President and Cook County Board of Commissioners express their support for the Major Richard Star Act and urge the United States Congress to enact legislation addressing the current offset affecting eligible combat-injured, medically retired service members; and 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that copies of this resolution be transmitted to the appropriate members of Congress representing Cook County to communicate the County’s support.

CONGRATULATING LAVERN MOORE ON  THE OCCASION OF HER RETIREMENT FROM COOK COUNTY GOVERNMENT

WHEREAS, LaVern Moore has been a dedicated and loyal public servant for Cook County Government for 34 years; and

WHEREAS, LaVern Moore began her career at Cook County in 1991 as a Commissary Line Worker and served in Sanitation in the Laundry Room prior to it being contracted for the Cook County Sheriff’s Department under President Richard Phelan. She subsequently worked under Presidents John H. Stroger, Bobbie L. Steele, Todd Stroger, and Toni Preckwinkle; and

WHEREAS, LaVern remained with the Cook County Sheriff’s Department until her transition to Janitorial Services within the Department of Facilities Management, where she began her tenure as a Janitor II; and

WHEREAS, LaVern served as Janitor II at the Domestic Violence Courthouse; and

WHEREAS, LaVern’s responsibilities under her current title as Janitor II included providing custodial services, assisting Community Service Officers as lead contact and liaison for the Domestic Violence Courthouse. LaVern also volunteered to assist building tenants with outreach programs; and

WHEREAS, LaVern recognizes the Apostolic Church of God in Christ as her home church, remains committed in her faith, and visits other churches from time to time; and

WHEREAS, LaVern is especially grateful and expresses her gratitude for the opportunity to serve Cook County and its residents over the past 34 years in her many roles, and has also served her community as a Precinct Captain for the 1st District and 2nd Ward in the 1990’s under Bobby L. Rush as well as Madeline Hitchcock; and

WHEREAS, LaVern is grateful to all co-workers and supervisors who supported her over the years and deserve as much credit for helping her reach the finish line. The friendships and relationships that were built, along with the many memories made, she will forever cherish; and

WHEREAS, LaVern appreciates many things, but her greatest love is the love she has for her family, including her daughter, Detective Maria A. Moore, a Twenty-four-year veteran of the Chicago Police Department, and her grandson, Masteal T. Harris, Jr., also a Chicago Police Officer for eight years serving in Main Control.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners does hereby congratulate LaVern Moore on her retirement and her service to Cook County...end

PROPOSED RESOLUTION

Holeman Owner, LLC CLASS 8 PROPERTY TAX INCENTIVE REQUEST 

WHEREAS, the Cook County Bureau of Economic Development received and reviewed a Real Property Assessment Classification 8 application containing the following information: 

Applicant: Holeman Owner, LLC 

Address: 3309 Holeman Avenue, South Chicago Heights, Illinois 

Municipality or Unincorporated Township: South Chicago Heights 

Cook County District: 6th District   

Permanent Index Number: 32-33-201-065-0000 

Municipal Resolution Number: Village of South Chicago Heights Resolution NO. 2025-R-11   

Number of month property vacant/abandoned: Number of months vacant 

Special circumstances justification requested: Yes 

Proposed use of property:  Industrial use- warehouse, manufacturing and distribution  

Living Wage Ordinance Compliance Affidavit Provided: Yes  

WHEREAS, the Cook County Board of Commissioners has adopted a Real Property Assessment Classification 8 that provides an applicant a reduction in the assessment level for an abandoned commercial facility; and

WHEREAS, the Cook County Classification System for Assessment defines abandoned property as buildings and other structures that, after having been vacant and unused for at least 12 continuous months, have been purchased for value by a purchaser in whom the seller has no direct financial interest; and

WHEREAS, in the instance where the property does not meet the definition of abandoned property, the municipality or the Board of Commissioners, may determine that special circumstances may exist that justify finding that the property is abandoned for purpose of Class 8; and

WHEREAS, in the case of abandonment of less than 12 months and purchase for value, by a purchaser in whom the seller has no direct financial interest, the County may determine that special circumstances justify finding the property is deemed abandoned; and

WHEREAS, Class 8 requires the validation by the County Board of the shortened period of qualifying abandonment in cases where the facility has been abandoned for less than 12 consecutive months upon purchase for value; and

WHEREAS, the municipality states the Class 8 is necessary for development to occur on this specific real estate. The municipal resolution cites the qualifications of this property to meet the definition of abandoned with special circumstances; and

WHEREAS; commercial real estate is normally assessed at 25% of its market value, qualifying commercial real estate eligible for the Class 8 can receive a significant reduction in the level of assessment from the date that new construction or rehabilitation has been completed, or in the case of abandoned property from the date of substantial re-occupancy.   Properties receiving Class 8 will be assessed at 10% of the market value for 10 years, 15% for the 11th year and 20% in the 12th year; and  

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, by the President and Board of Commissioners of the County of Cook, that the President and Board of Commissioners validate the above-captioned property is deemed abandoned with special circumstances under the Class 8; and 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the County Clerk is hereby authorized and directed to forward a certified copy of this resolution to the Office of the Cook County Assessor

This extension will ensure continuity of critical services and prevent any interruption in service delivery while maintaining compliance with the County’s procurement requirements.

The requested one year extension is a temporary measure to bridge the transition between the current contract and the anticipated new agreement resulting from the ongoing competitive procurement process.  

This contract was awarded through Request for Proposals (RFP) procedures in accordance with the Cook County Procurement Code. Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicina was selected based on established evaluation criteria.

il-17031-bos-matter-81069.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

AN INTERAGENCY GRANT AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE OFFICE OF THE CHIEF JUDGE AND THE COOK COUNTY JUSTICE ADVISORY COUNCIL AND A SUBRECIPIENT AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE OFFICE OF THE CHIEF JUDGE AND LURIE CHILDREN’S HOSPITAL FOR CONTINUATION OF THE JUVENILE JUSTICE COLLABORATIVE DEFERRED PROSECUTION PROGRAM 

WHEREAS, the Juvenile Justice Collaborative (“JJC”) is an evidence-based care coordination model consisting of a consortium of community-based agencies whose mission is to minimize future justice involvement for arrested youth and promote equity in the justice system; and 

WHEREAS, the JJC Deferred Prosecution Program (“JJC Program”) is an initiative of the JJC and the Cook County State’s Attorney’s Office that provides an alternative pathway from traditional prosecution for arrested youth; and 

WHEREAS, the JJC Program’s goals are (1) to reduce violence and minimize justice involvement of youth who have experienced past violence or trauma or are at increased risk of exposure to violence, and (2) to provide trauma-informed care coordination for justice-involved youth granted deferred prosecution; and 

WHEREAS, the JJC Program uses a community-based care coordination model that begins with an individual assessment to provide appropriate community-based mentorship, behavioral health treatment, educational services, family services, and job training for each youth’s needs; and  

WHEREAS, since 2017, Cook County Juvenile Probation Department and the Cook County State’s Attorney’s office (CCSAO) have referred over 1,500 youth to the JJC; and 

WHEREAS, an independent evaluation found that youth referred to the program, relative to a comparison group, were more than 40 percent less likely to reoffend at one year post referral; and 

WHEREAS, the County achieves its mission through strategic collaborations and partnerships with states, local governments, community organizations, and others; and  

WHEREAS, Lurie Children’s Hospital (“LCH”) is an established 501(c)(3) nonprofit agency, which has extensive experience and expertise in providing oversight of the JJC through comprehensive and coordinated community-based services, including the coordination of training, professional development, evaluation, and continuous quality improvement; and  

WHEREAS in 2022, the program expanded when the County allocated $6,109,124.00 in ARPA Funds to support efforts to reduce violence and minimize justice involvement among youth who have experienced violence or trauma or who are at high risk of exposure to violence, that was administered by OCJ to fund the work of LCH and the JJC Program via a subrecipient agreement between OCJ and LCH; and 

WHEREAS, LCH successfully administers the JJC Program as the “Partnership Steward,” providing coordination, program administration, evaluation, and strategic planning for the community-based organizations and service providers that contribute to the JJC Program; and 

WHEREAS, the JJC’s goals are greatly aligned with the Cook County Policy Roadmap pillar for Safe and Thriving communities, through the support of alternatives to detention and pathways to lesser involvement in the criminal legal system; and 

WHEREAS, in the furtherance of these Cook County goals, the Cook County Justice Advisory Council (JAC) engages in grantmaking in the areas of violence prevention, reentry services, and more with an eye toward investing in communities supporting success outside of the adult and juvenile justice systems; 

WHEREAS, the JAC has agreed to offer a grant to OCJ to help ensure that the work of the JJC can continue past the expiration of ARPA as it would further the goals of Cook County; and  

WHEREAS, the County, through OCJ and the JAC, wishes to continue funding and administering the JJC Program through November 30, 2027; and 

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners hereby authorizes the Justice Advisory Council (JAC) and the Office of the Chief Judge (OCJ) to enter an Interagency Agreement for the JAC to provide a grant of $1,000,000.00 to OCJ for the purposes of providing continued funding for the Juvenile Justice Collaborative Deferred Prosecution Program from October 22, 2026 through November 30, 2027; that the interagency agreement would have expenses accrued in FY26 and FY27; that the interagency agreement would designated the number 1205-IAAJJC-2026; and  

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners hereby authorizes OCJ to contribute an additional $350,000 to the Juvenile Justice Collaborative Deferred Prosecution Program; and the fiscal impacts across the two funding sources will be approximately $136,330.00 in FY26 and $1,213,670.00 in FY27; and 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners hereby authorizes OCJ to enter a subrecipient agreement with Lurie Children’s Hospital to continue administering the Juvenile Justice Collaborative Deferred Prosecution Fund as the Partnership Steward for up to $1,350,000 with a duration of October 22, 2026 through November 30, 2027, and under terms as required by the Interagency Agreement.

il-17031-bos-matter-81071.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

AUTHORIZATION FOR COOK COUNTY’S CONTINUED PARTICIPATION IN THE GREATER CHICAGOLAND ECONOMIC PARTNERSHIP (GCEP)

WHEREAS, in 2022 the elected officials of the seven counties of northeastern Illinois, the City of Chicago and corresponding economic development organizations (the Parties) agreed to partner and collaborate to advance economic development within the region; and 

WHEREAS, the Cook County Board approved Item 22-5730 authorizing the Chief of the Bureau of Economic Development, or his or her designee, to sign an agreement outlining the County’s annual financial contribution and the proposed scope of work to support a three-year pilot initiative; and 

WHEREAS, in 2025 the Parties clearly recognized positive outcomes for the Chicago region resulting from the pilot program, all Parties agreed to a one-year extension to develop a sustainable model to carry to organization forward; and 

WHEREAS, the Cook County Board approved Item 25-3921 continue and support GCEP through 2026 with funds in the Bureau of Economic Development’s FY 2025 budget; and 

WHEREAS, the Parties have agreed to leverage and build on the success of the pilot phase; and

WHEREAS, the Parties reaffirm their commitment to collaboratively advancing regional economic development by pursuing a unified approach to business development initiatives that promote inclusive growth, attract investment, strengthen systems and programs, and enhance Chicagoland’s global competitiveness; and

WHEREAS, to advance these objectives, the Parties will develop an Annual Workplan-approved by the GCEP Executive Committee-that outlines strategies to strengthen key economic sectors by retaining and expanding existing businesses, attracting new businesses, and showcasing the region’s economic development ecosystem in ways that promote inclusive and equitable growth; and

WHEREAS, the Annual Workplan will identify strategic priorities, membership engagement activities, program development, and outreach efforts, along with associated timelines and deliverables; and

WHEREAS, GCEP will annually develop and share key performance indicators (KPIs), goals, and objectives to measure partnership progress and overall effectiveness; and

WHEREAS, GCEP will continue to market the region, recognizing that a unified regional strategy benefits individual communities and projects across the partnership and supports broader regional prosperity; and

WHEREAS, as part of this next phase of organizational development, GCEP will establish an Executive Committee responsible for approving the Annual Workplan and the annual fundraising strategy; and

WHEREAS, the GCEP Executive Committee will also establish a Regional Advisory Committee, composed of the Executive Committee members and additional private-sector investors, to review and advise on strategies and priorities (See Attachment A); and

WHEREAS, World Business Chicago (WBC) will continue to administer the general operations of GCEP and provide staff support for the Regional Advisory Committee; and
WHEREAS, WBC will regularly provide a report outlining general economic development performance metrics, emerging opportunities, and related partnership activities; and

WHEREAS, Cook County will request that World Business Chicago (WBC) report to the Cook County Board Committee on Economic Development annually about GCEP’s impact; and

WHEREAS, each of the seven counties and the City of Chicago, acting through its agent World Business Chicago, have committed to the annual cost obligations set forth in Attachment B and shall provide the required contributions to support GCEP operations for the three-year period commencing in 2027; and

WHEREAS, the annual cost obligations for each participating jurisdiction have been determined pursuant to a formula that utilizes the arithmetic mean of the jurisdiction’s proportion of the region’s population and its proportion of regional employment; and

WHEREAS, the schedule of cost allocations for the 2027 program year, as calculated under this formula, is detailed in Attachment B; and

WHEREAS, the Cook County Board of Commissioners finds that continued participation in GCEP is in the best interests of the County and its residents, as it supports coordinated regional economic development, fosters inclusive growth, and enhances the region’s competitiveness.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners does authorize the Chief of Bureau of Economic Development or his or her designee to sign the 2027 GCEP Operating Agreement and to provide payment of $296,2745 annually to support GCEP operations for the 2027- 2029 calendar years.

il-17031-bos-matter-81081.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

RECOGNIZING SEPTEMBER AS OVARIAN CANCER AWARENESS MONTH IN COOK COUNTY
 
WHEREAS, ovarian cancer is the fifth leading cause of cancer deaths among women in the United States and causes more deaths than any other gynecologic cancer; and
 
WHEREAS, in the United States, a woman’s lifetime risk of being diagnosed with ovarian cancer is approximately 1 in 78; and
 
WHEREAS, the American Cancer Society estimates 21,010 cases of ovarian cancer will be newly diagnosed in 2026 and 12,450 individuals will die from the disease nationwide; and
 
WHEREAS, ovarian cancer is the deadliest of all female reproductive system cancers; and
 
WHEREAS, the five-year survival rate for ovarian cancer is over 90 percent for individuals diagnosed in early stages; and
 
WHEREAS, while mammograms can detect breast cancer and Pap smears may detect cervical cancer, there is no reliable early detection test for ovarian cancer; and
 
WHEREAS, in June 2007, the first national consensus statement on ovarian cancer symptoms was developed to provide consistency in describing symptoms to make it easier for women to learn and remember those symptoms; and
 
WHEREAS, Black women with ovarian cancer are more likely to have late-stage diagnoses, receive lower quality clinical services, and have lower five-year survival rates than non-Black women; and
 
WHEREAS, women of color, low-income women, and women living in rural areas face more barriers to accessing standard quality of care and are more likely to receive care at a facility that has poorer adherence to National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) treatment guidelines; and
 
WHEREAS, too many people remain unaware that the symptoms of ovarian cancer often include bloating, pelvic or abdominal pain, difficulty eating or feeling full quickly, urinary symptoms, and several other vague symptoms that are often easily confused with other diseases; and
 
WHEREAS, improved awareness of the symptoms of ovarian cancer by the public and healthcare providers may lead to quicker diagnoses; and
 
WHEREAS, half of the women who are diagnosed with ovarian cancer are 63 years or older according to the American Cancer Society; and

WHEREAS, the lack of an early detection test for ovarian cancer, combined with its vague symptoms, means that approximately 80 percent of cases of ovarian cancer are detected at an advanced stage; and
 
WHEREAS, persistent issues collecting and reporting data related to ovarian cancer risk, treatment, and outcomes are particularly pronounced and impede the development of effective policy; and
 
WHEREAS, all women are at risk for ovarian cancer, but approximately 20% of women who are diagnosed with ovarian cancer have a hereditary predisposition to ovarian cancer, which places them at higher risk; and
 
WHEREAS, scientists and physicians have uncovered changes in the BRCA genes that some women inherit from their parents, which may make those women 30 times more likely to develop ovarian cancer; and
 
WHEREAS, family history has been found to play an important role in accurately assessing the risk of developing ovarian cancer and medical experts believe that family history should be taken into consideration during an annual physician’s visits; and
 
WHEREAS, women who are at risk of ovarian cancer may undertake prophylactic measures, such as opportunistic salpingectomy, to help reduce the risk of developing this disease; and
 
WHEREAS, guidelines issued by the National Comprehensive Cancer Network and Society of Gynecologic Oncology recommend that individuals diagnosed with ovarian cancer receive genetic counseling and genetic testing regardless of their family history; and
 
WHEREAS, studies consistently show that compliance with these guidelines is alarmingly low, with recently published National Cancer Institute-funded research finding that in 2013 and 2014, only one-third of ovarian cancer survivors have undergone testing; and
 
WHEREAS, according to a 2016 consensus report by the National Academy of Medicine, “there remain surprising gaps in the fundamental knowledge about and understanding of ovarian cancer” across all aspects of the disease; and
 
WHEREAS, ongoing investments in ovarian cancer research and education and awareness efforts are critical to closing these gaps and improving survivorship for women with ovarian cancer; and
 
WHEREAS, annually in September, Ovarian Cancer Research Alliance (OCRA) and community partner organizations such as the National Ovarian Cancer Coalition, hold a number of events to increase public awareness of ovarian cancer and its symptoms; and
 
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, the month of September be hereby declared Ovarian Cancer Awareness Month in the County of Cook.

il-17031-bos-matter-81103.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

RECOGNITION OF THE WOMEN’S BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT CENTER’S 40TH ANNIVERSARY

WHEREAS, the Women’s Business Development Center (WBDC) was founded in 1986 by Hedy Ratner and S. Carol Dougal with a mission to expand economic opportunity for women and strengthen communities through business ownership; and

WHEREAS, in March 1986, the WBDC announcement its establishment of the nation’s first Small Business Development Center for Women marking an early milestone in its pioneering work to advance women entrepreneurs; and

WHEREAS, throughout its 40-year history, the WBDC has fostered bipartisan collaboration and built enduring partnerships among government leaders, corporate partners, nonprofit organizations and community stakeholders, continuing the founders’ commitment to bridging political and ideological divides in pursuit of expanding economic opportunity; and

WHEREAS, for four decades the WBDC has provided comprehensive support to business owners across the Midwest, including business advising, entrepreneurial training, access to capital, certification assistance and connections to contracting opportunities; and

WHEREAS, the WBDC has empowered more than 118,000 entrepreneurs from diverse backgrounds to achieve economic self-sufficiency through business creation, growth and long-term sustainability; and

WHEREAS, since its inception, the WBDC has delivered more than 15,000 entrepreneurial workshops and trainings designed to equip business owners with critical skills and tools for success; and

WHEREAS, the WBDC has helped women- and minority-owned businesses secure more than $185 million in financing, supporting business expansion, innovation and job creation across the region; and

WHEREAS, the WBDC has facilitated more than $1.15 billion in government and corporate contracting opportunities, enabling businesses to grow, contribute to local economies and strengthen communities; and

WHEREAS, each year the WBDC certifies nearly 2,500 Women Business Enterprises, ensuring that women-owned firms can access new market opportunities and participate competitively in supplier diversity programs; and

WHEREAS, headquartered in Chicago, the WBDC has grown from a local initiative into a nationally recognized leader in economic development, serving entrepreneurs across a nine-state region and helping pave the way for more than 160 women’s business centers nationwide; and

WHEREAS, the Women’s Business Development Center’s era of growth and expansion was guided by the exceptional leadership of Emilia DiMenco, who served for many years as President and Chief Executive Officer and recently retired, leaving a legacy of organizational strength, innovation and unwavering commitment to expanding economic opportunity for women and small businesses; and

WHEREAS, the Women’s Business Development Center has served as key partner to Cook County in establishing the Cook County Small Business Source, providing essential leadership and expertise that helped shape the program’s structure, services and impact; and

WHEREAS, during the COVID-19 pandemic, when Cook County faced unprecedented uncertainty and small businesses urgently needed support, the WBDC demonstrated a remarkable can-do spirit- assisting Cook County respond with timely guidance, relief navigation and technical assistance to businesses in crisis;

WHEREAS, the Women’s Business Development Center now enters a new chapter of leadership under Erica Kuhlman, the organization’s newly appointed President and Chief Executive Officer, who brings a deep commitment to entrepreneurial empowerment and will guide the WBDC as it continues to expand opportunity, strengthen communities and build on its 40-year legacy of impact; and

WHEREAS, in 2026 the WBDC celebrates its 40th anniversary, marking four decades of empowering entrepreneurs, advancing economic equity and supporting community vitality throughout Cook County and beyond;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners hereby recognizes and celebrates the 40th anniversary of the Women’s Business Development Center and honors its continued commitment to expanding economic opportunity, strengthening communities and supporting the next generation of entrepreneurs; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners extends its gratitude to the founders, staff, partners and thousands of entrepreneurs who have contributed to the WBDC’s enduring legacy of service and impact; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that a suitable copy of this Resolution be presented to the Women’s Business Development Center in recognition of this milestone anniversary and its 40 years of transformative contributions to Cook County and the region.

il-17031-bos-matter-81104.title:
PROPOSED GRANT AWARD 

Department:  Cook County Health 

Grantee:  Cook County Health 

Grantor:  Department of Health and Human Services/Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services/ Administration Center for Mental Health Services

Request: Authorization to accept grant  

Purpose:  Cook County Health Children’s Mental Health Initiative 

Grant Amount:  $999,999.00 

Grant Period:  9/30/2026-9/29/2027

Fiscal Impact:  None 

Accounts: 41215.4896.10755

Concurrences: 
The Budget Department has received all requisite documents and determined the fiscal impact on Cook County, if any.

Summary:  This is a formal request to accept the Cook County Health Children’s Mental Health Initiative Grant. Cook County faces a severe youth behavioral health crisis. In 2023, more than 30,000 minors required behavioral health hospitalization in Chicago, and over 1,100 youth died by suicide between 2019 and 2023. Despite increasing demand, many youth do not receive timely care due to fragmentation and limited access. CareConnect Youth (CCY) addresses these challenges by establishing a coordinated infrastructure that connects identification to care. CCY is a community-based, school-linked system of care designed to improve access to behavioral health services for children, youth, and young adults (ages 0-21) with serious emotional disturbance (SED) and those at risk in Cook County, Illinois. Led by the Cook County Health Office of Behavioral Health (OBH) in partnership with Open Roads Behavioral Health a network of schools, health systems, and community organizations, CCY addresses critical gaps, including fragmented referral pathways, long wait times, and limited care coordination. The initiative will be implemented in high-need communities served by Chicago Public Schools (CPS) and Noble Schools, which collectively serve over 328,000 students, most of whom are Medicaid-insured. These settings provide a critical entry point for reaching youth with serious emotional disturbance (SED) and those at risk, particularly as Illinois prepares to implement universal school-based mental health screening for students in grades 3-12 beginning in the 2027-2028 school year following passage of Illinois SB1560, as demand will rapidly expand. CCY will implement a hub-based model beginning in North Lawndale, Chicago in Year 1, with expansion of hubs in Years 2-4. Each hub will serve as a single point of access supported by a centralized referral system, including an intake coordinator, telephone line, and web-based portal. Through a provider network, CCY will ensure access to a full continuum of services, including outpatient therapy, crisis response, intensive home-based services, day treatment, and care coordination. Services will be delivered using evidence-based practices, supported by a tiered care coordination model, including High-Fidelity Wraparound for youth with complex needs. CCY is guided by three core goals: increase timely access to care; improve clinical outcomes; and strengthen system integration. By Year 4, CCY will provide care coordination to 800 youth annually and deliver mental health services to 400 youth annually. Key targets include contacting 90% of referred youth within 5 days, linking 90% to treatment within 30 days, and achieving clinically meaningful improvement for at least 60% of youth within six months. The initiative includes a system of care Governance Board, cross-system partnerships, and a sustainability strategy anchored in Medicaid reimbursement and integration into OBH infrastructure. By aligning identification, referral, and service delivery, CCY will improve outcomes, reduce fragmentation, and establish a sustainable system of care ensuring youth and families receive timely, coordinated, and evidence-based support.
