il-17031-bos-matter-81126.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION


A RESOLUTION HONORING COURT APPOOINTED SPECIAL ADVOCATES (CASA) OF COOK COUNTY FOR ITS EXTRAORDINARY ADVOCACY ON BEHALF OF CHILDREN AND YOUTH IN FOSTER CARE

WHEREAS, pursuant to the Illinois Juvenile Court Act, (705ILCS 405/2-17.1) Court Appointed Special Advocates (CASA) serve as trained advocates appointed by the court to represent the best interests of children involved in abuse and neglect proceedings; and

WHEREAS, Court Appointed Special Advocates (CASA) of Cook County, founded in 1986, is a nonprofit organization dedicated to ensuring that children involved in the foster care system have their rights protected, their voices heard, and their best interests advanced through advocacy that promotes safety, permanency, well-being, and successful transitions to adulthood; and

WHEREAS, for more than forty years, CASA of Cook County has provided unwavering advocacy and support to more than 12,000 children and youth affected by abuse, neglect, family instability, trauma, and prolonged involvement in the child welfare system; and

WHEREAS, as one of the nation's largest and most complex urban CASA programs, and the only organization of its kind serving children within the Cook County Juvenile Court system, CASA of Cook County fulfills a unique and indispensable role by providing highly trained volunteer advocates who serve as independent voices for children in court proceedings and throughout their child welfare journeys; and

WHEREAS, children involved in the foster care system often face significant challenges related to physical and mental health, educational attainment, housing stability, and emotional wellbeing, and research has demonstrated that children assigned a CASA volunteer experience improved outcomes and are more likely to achieve permanency and stability; and

WHEREAS, African American children remain disproportionately represented within the foster care system and frequently experience longer stays in care and greater barriers to permanency, underscoring the importance of CASA's advocacy on behalf of children and families impacted by longstanding inequities and systemic challenges; and

WHEREAS, CASA of Cook County has undergone extraordinary growth and transformation in recent years, expanding its reach seventeen-fold since 2018 and achieving the largest service footprint in the organization's history, ensuring that more children than ever before have access to a dedicated advocate; and

WHEREAS, CASA of Cook County has demonstrated leadership and innovation through the development of specialized initiatives, including the Early Childhood Court Team (Safe Babies Court), the Medically At-Risk Kids (M.A.R.K.) Program, and the Creating Independent
Transitions for Youth (C.I.T.Y.) Program, all of which provide targeted support to some of the County's most vulnerable children and youth; and

WHEREAS, in partnership with the Juvenile Court of Cook County, CASA of Cook County has advanced groundbreaking reforms designed to strengthen family preservation, improve permanency outcomes, and ensure greater accountability and support for youth transitioning out of foster care; and

WHEREAS, through the dedication of its staff, volunteers, supporters, and community partners, CASA of Cook County has transformed the lives of thousands of children and youth by promoting safety, stability, educational success, access to healthcare, family connections, and long-term well-being; and

WHEREAS, the Cook County Board of Commissioners recognizes the invaluable contributions of CASA volunteers and staff whose compassion, service, and commitment help ensure that every child has the opportunity to reach their full potential; and 

NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the President of the Cook County Board and the Cook County Board of Commissioners do hereby honor and recognize Court Appointed Special Advocates (CASA) of Cook County for its extraordinary commitment to advocating for the best interests of children and youth in foster care and for its enduring contributions to the well-being of the residents of Cook County; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners expresses its sincere gratitude to the staff, volunteers, supporters, and community partners of CASA of Cook County for their dedication to ensuring that every child has a safe, stable, and supportive future; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that a suitable copy of this Resolution be presented to Court Appointed Special Advocates (CASA) of Cook County as a symbol of the respect, appreciation, and admiration of the President and Members of the Cook County Board of Commissioners.

il-17031-bos-matter-81127.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

HONORING RAMI DOUKKY FOR 31 YEARS OF DISTINGUISHED SERVICE TO COOK COUNTY HEALTH

WHEREAS, Dr. Rami Doukky, MD, MSc, MBA, has devoted 31 years of distinguished service to Cook County Health, beginning his career at the historic Cook County Hospital in 1995 and serving as an attending cardiologist since 2002; and

WHEREAS, Dr. Doukky served as Chairman of the Division of Cardiology from 2014 to 2024, providing visionary leadership that strengthened cardiovascular care, education, research, and quality throughout Cook County Health; and

WHEREAS, in 2022, Dr. Doukky became the Founding Medical Director of the Cook County Health Cardiovascular Service Line, where he developed and implemented a comprehensive system of cardiovascular services, including advanced cardiac imaging, structural heart disease, electrophysiology, pulmonary embolism intervention, lipid and cardiovascular genetics, and specialized HIV cardiovascular care; and

WHEREAS, under his leadership, Cook County Health achieved national recognition for cardiovascular quality and excellence, including the National Association of Counties Achievement Award in 2024 and the American Heart Association Commitment to Quality Award in 2025; and

WHEREAS, in recognition of his academic accomplishments and contributions to medicine, Dr. Doukky was appointed Professor of Medicine and Radiology at Rush Medical College in 2014; and

WHEREAS, Dr. Doukky has made significant contributions to medical education and research, mentoring hundreds of trainees and physicians, authoring more than 170 peer-reviewed publications, and serving as principal investigator on grants totaling more than $1 million; and

WHEREAS, Dr. Doukky’s leadership extends nationally through his service as Vice President of the American Society of Nuclear Cardiology and his upcoming service as President in 2028; and

WHEREAS, Dr. Doukky’s career reflects an unwavering commitment to advancing cardiovascular care and ensuring equitable access to high-quality medical services for all Cook County residents, regardless of their ability to pay; and

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the President and Members of the Cook County Board of Commissioners hereby honor Dr. Rami Doukky, MD, MSc, MBA, for his 31 years of exceptional service, leadership, scholarship, mentorship, and dedication to the health and well-being of the residents of Cook County; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners commends Dr. Doukky for his lasting contributions to Cook County Health and cardiovascular medicine and extends its sincere appreciation for his distinguished public service.

il-17031-bos-matter-81139.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

RESOLUTION HONORING MICHAEL W. LEWIS FOR HIS SERVICE TO THE REGIONAL TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY 

WHEREAS, Michael W. Lewis was appointed to the Board of Directors of the Regional Transportation Authority (RTA) in November 2013, representing suburban Cook County; and 

WHEREAS, Mr. Lewis has served the RTA with distinction for more than a decade, including in his role as Vice-Chair of the Audit Committee and as a member of the Finance Committee, providing steady leadership and thoughtful oversight of the Authority’s financial stewardship and accountability; and 

WHEREAS, Mr. Lewis brought to the RTA a wealth of corporate experience from his more than 30-year career with BMO Financial Group, where he served in numerous roles including assistant vice-president, vice-president, and team leader in the Special Industries Group, assuming responsibility for the Healthcare, Education, and Tax-Exempt Institutions Team; and 

WHEREAS, Mr. Lewis concluded his distinguished corporate career as Regional President and Executive Vice President of the Chicago Metro Region of BMO Harris Bank, roles in which he managed critical operations, strategic growth, and community engagement across the region; and 

WHEREAS, Mr. Lewis has been an active civic leader in his community, serving on the Village of Olympia Fields’ Economic Development Committee, participating on the zoning board of appeals, contributing to the BMO Harris Diversity Council, and co-chairing the sustainability council; and 

WHEREAS, Mr. Lewis has further contributed to the advancement of higher education through his service on Western Michigan University’s Foundation Board and as chairman of the Dean’s Advisory Council for the Haworth College of Business; and 

WHEREAS, Mr. Lewis’s broad professional expertise, commitment to public service, and dedication to equitable and sustainable community development have strengthened the work of the RTA and enhanced regional mobility throughout northeastern Illinois; and 

WHEREAS, Mr. Lewis was one of the advocates for better funding for the transit system through reforms such as Northeastern Illinois Transit Authority (NITA), contributing to the development and advancement of the legislation that underpins this new regional governance structure, provides sustainable funding to strengthen the future of public transportation in northeastern Illinois; and 

WHEREAS, during his tenure, Mr. Lewis consistently demonstrated integrity, vision, and a deep commitment to ensuring that public transportation remains accessible, fiscally responsible, and aligned with the needs of the region’s residents; and 

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that we do hereby acknowledge and express our gratitude for Michael W. Lewis’s years of service to the Regional Transportation Authority, recognize his many contributions to public transportation and civic leadership, and extend our best wishes to him in all future endeavors.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that a suitable copy of this Resolution be spread upon the official proceedings of this Honorable Body, and that an official copy of same be tendered to Michael W. Lewis.

il-17031-bos-matter-81140.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

RESOLUTION HONORING RICK KWASNESKI FOR A LIFETIME OF PUBLIC SERVICE 

WHEREAS, Chairman Rick Kwasneski was originally appointed to the Pace Board on August 28, 2002 as the representative from Southwest Cook County, and then was appointed Chairman of the Pace Board on December 7, 2006, becoming the third and longest-serving chairman in Pace’s history; and 

WHEREAS, Chairman Kwasneski’s advocacy to the Illinois General Assembly enabled Pace to thrive, resulting in legislation that increased Pace funding in both 2008 and 2025; and 

WHEREAS, Chairman Kwasneski’s vision for express bus-on-shoulder service led to a 2011 change in State law that makes Pace the sole operator of buses on the shoulder of Interstate 55 in the southwest suburbs and which led to 600% ridership growth in that corridor over the first seven years of the service; and 

WHEREAS, Chairman Kwasneski led the development of Pace’s Pulse rapid transit program and the launch of the first two lines, on Milwaukee Avenue in 2019, and on Dempster Street in 2023, with another four lines currently in development; and 

WHEREAS, Chairman Kwasneski’s focus on Pace’s role in economic development led to the construction of a new Acceptance Facility and a new Central Safety & Training and Customer Service Facility, both in Markham, and a new Heritage Division in Plainfield, Pace’s first new operating garage in more than 30 years; and 

WHEREAS, Chairman Kwasneski’s vision for improving the facilities Pace’s customers use on a daily basis led to the largest infrastructure program in Pace’s history, including a new park-n-ride in Plainfield, a new Joliet Transit Center, and an expanded Northwest Transportation Center; and 

WHEREAS, Chairman Kwasneski’s commitment to innovation led to the development of the Call-n-Ride program, later rebranded as On Demand, which has now spread to eleven different suburban zones, as well as the launch of the VanGo program, which has spread to eight different suburban zones, and the creation of the Taxi Access and Rideshare Access Programs for Paratransit-certified customers; and 

WHEREAS, Chairman Kwasneski’s twenty-year tenure resulted in Pace providing nearly 600 million total trips to northeastern Illinois commuters, ensuring that an average of one hundred thousand people per day were able to access employment, education, medical services and leisure activities in our region as a result of his leadership; and 

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that we do hereby acknowledge Chairman Kwasneski’s accomplishments, express our gratitude for his years of dedicated service, and extend our best wishes to him in all future endeavors.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that a suitable copy of this Resolution be spread upon the official proceedings of this Honorable Body, and that an official copy of same be tendered to Chairman Rick Kwasneski.

PROPOSED RESOLUTION

Wolf Family Enterprises, LLC 6B PROPERTY TAX INCENTIVE REQUEST 

WHEREAS, the Cook County Bureau of Economic Development received and reviewed a Real Property Assessment Classification 6b application containing the following information: 

Applicant: Wolf Family Enterprises, LLC 

Address: 1201 Busse Rd, Elk Grove Village, Illinois  

Municipality or Unincorporated Township: Elk Grove Village 

Cook County District: 15th District    

Permanent Index Number: 08-26-303-013-0000  

Municipal Resolution Number: Village of Elk Grove, Resolution No. 33-35  

Number of month property vacant/abandoned: 12 months vacant 

Special circumstances justification requested: Yes  

Proposed use of property:  Industrial use - warehousing, manufacturing, and distribution 

Living Wage Ordinance Compliance Affidavit Provided: Yes    

WHEREAS, the Cook County Board of Commissioners has adopted a Real Property Assessment Classification 6b that provides an applicant a reduction in the assessment level for an abandoned industrial facility; and

WHEREAS, the Cook County Classification System for Assessment defines abandoned property as buildings and other structures that, after having been vacant and unused for at least 12 continuous months, have been purchased for value by a purchaser in whom the seller has no direct financial interest; and

WHEREAS, in the instance where the property does not meet the definition of abandoned property, the municipality or the Board of Commissioners, may determine that special circumstances may exist that justify finding that the property is abandoned for purpose of Class 6b; and

WHEREAS, in the case of abandonment of less than 12 months and purchase for value, by a purchaser in whom the seller has no direct financial interest, the County may determine that special circumstances justify finding the property is deemed abandoned; and

WHEREAS, Class 6b requires the validation by the County Board of the shortened period of qualifying abandonment in cases where the facility has been abandoned for less than 12 consecutive months upon purchase for value; and

WHEREAS, the municipality states the Class 6b is necessary for development to occur on this specific real estate. The municipal resolution cites the qualifications of this property to meet the definition of abandoned with special circumstances; and

WHEREAS, industrial real estate is normally assessed at 25% of its market value, qualifying industrial real estate eligible for the Class 6b can receive a significant reduction in the level of assessment from the date that new construction or rehabilitation has been completed, or in the case of abandoned property from the date of substantial re-occupancy.   Properties receiving Class 6b will be assessed at 10% of the market value for 10 years, 15% for the 11th year and 20% in the 12th year; and  

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, by the President and Board of Commissioners of the County of Cook, that the President and Board of Commissioners validate the above-captioned property is deemed abandoned with special circumstances under the Class 6b; and 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the County Clerk is hereby authorized and directed to forward a certified copy of this resolution to the Office of the Cook County Assessor

il-17031-bos-matter-81149.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

OPPOSING THE PROPOSED AMTRAK MIDWEST MAINTENANCE FACILITY AT THE UNION PACIFIC CANAL YARD AND CALLING FOR COMPREHENSIVE ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW AND MEANINGFUL COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT

WHEREAS, Amtrak is proposing to construct a Midwest Maintenance Facility at the Union Pacific Canal Yard in Chicago, supported by up to $572 million in federal funding, along with an additional $87 million for related Canal Street bridge and viaduct improvements; and

WHEREAS, the proposed facility and associated rail traffic would directly affect the communities of Chinatown, Pilsen, Armour Square, Bronzeville and Bridgeport, with residents, schools, senior housing, parks, and other community institutions in these neighborhoods potentially experiencing the project’s environmental, noise, traffic, and quality-of-life impacts; and

WHEREAS, the proposed facility would be a major rail maintenance operation that could operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week, immediately adjacent to the heavily used Armour Square Park, just a few blocks from the Illinois Institute of Technology (IIT) campus and the Armour Square Senior Homes, T.E. Brown Senior Apartments, Wentworth Gardens Homes and within approximately one mile of numerous schools, including Robert Healy Elementary School, Minnie Miñoso Academy, Air Force Academy High School, Armour Elementary School, Bridgeport Catholic Academy and De La Salle Institute; and

WHEREAS, at its current location, Amtrak trains make relatively short trips to and from Chicago’s Union Station. Moving the maintenance facility farther south would require trains to travel farther for fueling, cleaning, catering and maintenance. Those additional movements would pass through the already busy rail corridor at 21st Street Bridge and Alton Junction, where Amtrak, Metra and freight trains share the tracks. With nearly 100 trains using the bridge each day, adding more Amtrak movements could increase congestion, make an already complex rail system more difficult to operate, and cause additional train idling and pollution concerns; and

WHEREAS, the proposed project raises significant concerns regarding diesel locomotive emissions and particulate matter, noise, vibration, hazardous materials, fuel and wastewater, stormwater runoff, potential soil and groundwater contamination, industrial lighting, construction impacts, and the cumulative environmental impacts associated with existing and proposed railroad and transportation activities; and

WHEREAS, the residents of the surrounding neighborhoods, including Armour Square, Chinatown, Bridgeport, Pilsen and Bronzeville, along with the surrounding communities, deserve a transparent and meaningful opportunity to understand, evaluate and participate in decisions concerning a project that could have permanent environmental and quality-of-life consequences for their neighborhoods; and

WHEREAS, the Cook County Board of Commissioners recognizes the importance of protecting the health, safety, environment and quality of life of Cook County residents and believes that major infrastructure projects receiving substantial public funding should be subject to rigorous environmental review, transparency and meaningful community participation.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners hereby expresses its opposition to the proposed Amtrak Midwest Maintenance Facility at the Union Pacific Canal Yard in its current form and location due to significant environmental, health, safety and quality-of-life concerns; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners calls upon Amtrak and the appropriate federal, state and local agencies to pause further advancement of the project until a comprehensive assessment of its potential environmental and community impacts has been completed and made available for public review; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the environmental review should specifically evaluate air quality and diesel particulate matter, noise, vibration, stormwater, hazardous materials, wastewater, soil and groundwater, traffic, lighting, construction impacts, and the cumulative effects of the proposed facility together with existing railroad and transportation activities in the surrounding community; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners urges the Illinois Environmental Protection Agency, the United States Environmental Protection Agency and the Federal Railroad Administration to conduct rigorous environmental and regulatory review of the proposed project to ensure that all applicable environmental protections and public participation requirements are fully satisfied; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners urges Amtrak to work with the affected communities and their elected representatives to identify reasonable alternatives and project modifications that would prevent or substantially reduce adverse environmental and quality-of-life impacts; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that suitable copies of this Resolution shall be transmitted to Amtrak; the Federal Railroad Administration; the United States Environmental Protection Agency; the Illinois Environmental Protection Agency; the Governor of the State of Illinois; the Attorney General of the State of Illinois; the Mayor of the City of Chicago; the Illinois Sports Facility Authority; the members of the Illinois Congressional Delegation; and other appropriate governmental and regulatory authorities.

il-17031-bos-matter-81151.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

HONORING THE 80TH BIRTHDAY OF PROFESSOR SHAFFDEEN A. AMUWO


WHEREAS, Professor Shaffdeen A. Amuwo, born on September 15, 1946, in Lagos, Nigeria, and Professor Emeritus at the University of Illinois at Chicago (UIC) School of Public Health, is a globally renowned advocate, humanitarian, and scholar of public health and equity in healthcare and education whose decades of leadership, service, and vision have transformed thousands of lives in the United States, Nigeria, and several other countries; and

WHEREAS, Professor Amuwo is a proud son of Lagos, educated at Zumratul Islamiyyah Elementary School and Methodist Boys’ High School, having attended evening classes and worked at the United Bank for Africa prior to continuing his studies in the United States; and

WHEREAS, Professor Amuwo is a paternal descendant of the Royal Family of the Eletu Iwashe of Lagos and a maternal grandson of Chief Sadiku Sarumi, the Ashoju Oba of Lagos during the reign of Oba Adele; and

WHEREAS, Professor Amuwo has played a critical role in laying the foundation for the groundbreaking Pipelines/Pathways to Health Professions training program, which introduced thousands of young people to futures in healthcare, public health, and related sectors; and

WHEREAS, over his illustrious and impactful career, Professor Amuwo has become known as a “Public Health Bridge Builder Extraordinaire,” receiving national and international recognition for his pioneering work to open doors for Nigerians, African-Americans, and others from underrepresented backgrounds seeking to enter the health professions; and

WHEREAS, Professor Amuwo has played a major part in several medical and public health missions which have facilitated the donation of over US$50 million worth in critical supplies such as medical equipment and eyeglasses to several African countries, including Nigeria, Ghana, and South Africa; and

WHEREAS, he has continued his legacy of mentorship and empowerment uplifting several generations of aspiring health professionals from the Nigerian-American and African-American communities, helping to build a diverse pipeline of public health and healthcare leaders across borders; and

WHEREAS, Professor Amuwo continues to serve as Chairman of Africa International House, supporting initiatives such as the African Festival of the Arts, the largest annual event highlighting African arts and culture in the State of Illinois; and

WHEREAS, he continues to serve as Chairman of the Board of Trustees of the Nigerian Islamic Association, as well as on the Board of Trustees of the Light of Islam, as well as on the Governing Council of Lagos State University; and

WHEREAS, he has acted as a critical ambassador between the vibrant Nigerian, African-American, and diaspora communities in Cook County and abroad, promoting inclusive and innovative solutions to pressing public health challenges via initiatives such as the establishment of the Lagos State Centre for Disease Control; and

WHEREAS, Professor Amuwo has been happily married to Linda Marie Amuwo for over four decades, and together they are blessed with children who continue to distinguish themselves in their respective professions; and

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners does hereby honor and commend Professor Shaffdeen A. Amuwo on the occasion of his 80th birthday, recognizing his outstanding service and enduring dedication to the health and well-being of communities throughout Cook County, the State of Illinois, and around the world; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that a suitable copy of this Resolution be prepared and presented to Professor Shaffdeen A. Amuwo and his family as an expression of the Cook County Board of Commissioners’ sincere gratitude for his extraordinary lifetime of service, scholarship, leadership, and lasting impact on the health and well-being of countless individuals and communities.

il-17031-bos-matter-81163.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

RECOGNIZING BLOOD CANCER AND SICKLE CELL AWARENESS MONTH IN COOK COUNTY

WHEREAS, the month of September is National Blood Cancer and Sickle Cell Awareness Month, a month-long initiative designated by Congress to help focus attention on the need for research and treatment of blood cancer and sickle cell diseases; and

WHEREAS, Sickle cell disease (SCD) is the most common inherited blood disorder in the United States, in which red blood cells may become sickle-shaped and harden. For a baby to be born with sickle cell disease, both parents must carry a sickle cell trait or gene. Sickle cell disease is not contagious, and there is no universal cure; and

WHEREAS, about 1 in 13 African Americans carry the sickle cell trait, and many do not know they have it; an estimated 100,000 people in the U.S. have SCD, with approximately 2,000 babies born with SCD annually in the United States; and

WHEREAS, people of many ethnic backgrounds can have SCD, but it disproportionately affects Black and Brown Americans, with more than 90% of U.S. cases occurring in non-Hispanic Black or African American individuals, and an estimated 3%-9% occurring in Hispanic or Latino individuals; and

WHEREAS, sickle cell disease leads to complications including chronic, severe, and unpredictable pain, anemia, frequent infections, swelling in the extremities, fatigue, and delayed growth, and was identified as an underlying medical condition associated with increased risk of severe illness from COVID-19, including hospitalization, ICU admission, intubation or mechanical ventilation, or death; and

WHEREAS, this national focus reinforces the National Institutes of Health's (NIH) continued support of SCD research, education, and capacity building, including the "Cure Sickle Cell Initiative" to accelerate safe, effective, and scalable gene therapies to cure the disease; and

WHEREAS, because of advances and medical breakthroughs in genetic therapies and research, new curative options for sickle cell disease are now reaching patients outside of clinical trials - including a gene therapy shown in its pivotal trial to eliminate severe pain crises in the large majority of treated patients; and

WHEREAS, in December 2023, the FDA approved the first two cell-based gene therapies for sickle cell disease, Casgevy and Lyfgenia, for patients aged 12 and older; previously, the only options for people with sickle cell disease were treatments to manage symptoms or donor stem cell transplants, which carry serious risks; and

WHEREAS, in July 2025, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) announced that 35 jurisdictions - 33 states, including the State of Illinois, plus the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico - had joined its new, voluntary Cell and Gene Therapy Access Model, under which the federal government has negotiated "outcomes-based agreements" with cell and gene therapy manufacturers so that state Medicaid agencies can deliver these treatments to people with sickle cell disease; and

WHEREAS, an international clinical trial has advanced another curative option for sickle cell disease: haploidentical bone marrow transplant using thiotepa and posttransplant cyclophosphamide, an approach researchers have identified as a safer and more affordable alternative to myeloablative gene therapy and gene-editing treatments for many patients; and

WHEREAS, results from this international, multicenter phase 2 trial, published June 20, 2024 in the American Society of Hematology's journal Blood, showed a two-year overall survival rate of 94.1%, with no difference in outcomes between children and adults; and

WHEREAS, individuals can help be part of the solution by donating blood, which remains one of the most valuable treatments for sickle cell patients, but less than 10% of Americans donate blood, and only about 5% of blood donors are of African ancestry, even though sickle cell patients benefit most from transfusions closely matched to their own ethnic background; and

WHEREAS, education and research - including learning about sickle cell disease and sickle cell trait, and getting tested for sickle cell trait if you are of African descent and do not know your status - are other ways to contribute to this important cause; and

WHEREAS, blood cancers - including leukemia, lymphoma, myeloma, and Hodgkin's disease - are among the world's most prevalent and dangerous cancers, and every 3 minutes, someone in the U.S. is diagnosed with a blood cancer; more than 1.3 million Americans are living with or in remission from a blood cancer; and

WHEREAS, blood cancers are the 3rd leading cause of cancer deaths in the U.S., but many people don't know the impact of blood cancers such as leukemia, lymphoma, and myeloma, and despite progress, more than one-third of blood cancer patients still do not survive five years after diagnosis; and

WHEREAS, giving blood is also important for blood cancer patients; although blood transfusions do not treat the blood cancer itself, they provide healthy blood cells when a patient's body isn't producing its own, helping relieve symptoms and side effects; and

WHEREAS, additionally, for patients diagnosed with leukemia, lymphoma, and other life-threatening diseases, a bone marrow or cord blood transplant may be their best or only hope for a cure; however, about 70% of patients who need a transplant do not have a fully matched donor in their family, which is why it's important to encourage people to sign up as potential donors; and

WHEREAS, the disparities faced by blood cancer patients mirror disparities faced broadly in the United States, with minority groups disproportionately affected across different blood cancer diseases, including higher incidence rates - for example, Black Americans have more than double the incidence of multiple myeloma compared with other races or ethnicities; and

WHEREAS, among people under the age of 20, Hispanics have the highest rate of leukemia of any ethnicity - in children, by more than 20%; and

WHEREAS, this Honorable Body wishes to promote and raise awareness of Blood Cancer and Sickle Cell Diseases in Cook County and encourage everyone to be a part of this national effort to increase awareness about blood cancer and sickle cell diseases during the month of September, and to stand united to improve the health of those living with them;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the President and the Cook County Board of Commissioners, on behalf of the more than 5.2 million residents of Cook County, do hereby take this opportunity to acknowledge Blood Cancer and Sickle Cell Awareness Month; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that in conjunction with National Blood Cancer and Sickle Cell Awareness Month, that the month of September 2026 be hereby declared Blood Cancer and Sickle Cell Awareness Month in the County of Cook; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that this text be spread upon the official proceedings of this Honorable Body.

il-17031-bos-matter-81164.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

HONORING HAZEL CREST POLICE CHIEF MITCHELL R. DAVIS III FOR HIS DISTINGUISHED CAREER IN LAW ENFORCEMENT AND NATIONAL LEADERSHIP

WHEREAS, the Cook County Board of Commissioners is pleased to recognize Mitchell R. Davis III, Chief of Police for the Village of Hazel Crest, for his distinguished career in law enforcement, commitment to public service, and recent installation as the 49th National President of the National Organization of Black Law Enforcement Executives (NOBLE); and

WHEREAS, Chief Davis has dedicated decades to protecting and serving communities throughout the South Suburbs, beginning his law enforcement career with the Park Forest Police Department and later serving as Chief of Police for the Villages of Dixmoor and Hazel Crest; and

WHEREAS, Chief Davis has demonstrated exceptional leadership throughout his career, including serving as the 73rd President of the Illinois Association of Chiefs of Police, becoming the first black President of that organization; and

WHEREAS, Chief Davis has held numerous leadership positions with NOBLE and now serves as its National President, continuing the organization's mission of advancing justice, equity, accountability, and meaningful relationships between law enforcement and the communities they serve; and

WHEREAS, Chief Davis has been a strong advocate for community engagement, mentorship, and collaborative approaches to public safety, including efforts to address gun violence and strengthen trust between law enforcement and residents; and

WHEREAS, Chief Davis has served on statewide boards and commissions, including the Illinois Commission on Discrimination and Hate Crimes and the Illinois Law Enforcement Training and Standards Board, and has been recognized for his contributions to law enforcement and public service; and

WHEREAS, Chief Davis has worked alongside Cook County Commissioner Donna Miller on efforts to address gun violence and improve public safety throughout the South Suburbs and Cook County, reflecting a shared commitment to collaboration and community well-being; and

WHEREAS, Chief Davis' appointment to lead NOBLE on the national level is a significant achievement for the Village of Hazel Crest, the South Suburbs, Cook County, and the State of Illinois, and is a testament to his decades of service, leadership, and dedication.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the President and Members of the Cook County Board of Commissioners, on behalf of the residents of Cook County, hereby honor and congratulate Chief Mitchell R. Davis III on his distinguished career in law enforcement and his installation as the 49th National President of the National Organization of Black Law Enforcement Executives; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners commends Chief Davis for his groundbreaking leadership, including his historic service as the first Black President of the Illinois Association of Chiefs of Police, and for his continued commitment to justice, equitable policing, community engagement, and public safety; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that a suitable copy of this resolution be presented to Chief Mitchell R. Davis III as a symbol of the Cook County Board of Commissioners' appreciation and congratulations on this distinguished achievement.

il-17031-bos-matter-81203.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

HONORING DR. PEGGY A. MONTES ON THE OCCASION OF HER 90TH BIRTHDAY

WHEREAS, Dr. Peggy A. Montes is a native Chicagoan born on October 17, 1936, who has devoted her life to serving women, girls and disadvantaged children, with a philanthropic and volunteer career centered on Empowering Women and Educating Children; and

WHEREAS, Peggy left teaching to found and lead multiple institutions, and is best known as the Founder and President of the Bronzeville Children’s Museum - still the first and only African American children’s museum in the country - now celebrating its 33rd Anniversary, and as a civic, cultural, educational and women’s rights activist who serves on numerous boards, commissions and committees; and

WHEREAS, a lifelong volunteer, Dr. Montes made history as the first female Chairman of the Board of Trustees and Building Committee at the DuSable Museum of African American History, where Dr. Margaret T. Burroughs was her mentor and best friend, and led the development and completion of the $3.5 million Harold Washington Wing; and

WHEREAS, her museum involvements include as co-founding member of the Chicago Art Institute Leadership Advisory Council, member of the Black Creativity Council of the Museum of Science and Industry, twenty-seven-year member of the Illinois Arts Council, member of the Illinois Book Advisory Committee, and founding member of Leadership Illinois - a women’s empowerment organization celebrating its 36th Anniversary that encourages women to become politically active; and

WHEREAS, Dr. Montes served on the Board of Trustees of Provident Hospital from 1980 to 1987, helping spearhead the completion and opening of the new Provident Hospital in 1986, and served over thirteen years on the Board of Trustees of Chicago State University, as one of the first Trustees appointed in 1996 and as Board Chairman from 2005 to 2007, during which she worked with architects to redesign the fourth floor Sunroom in the Gwendolyn Brooks Library; and

WHEREAS, Dr. Montes also worked with Dr. Frances Carroll, Senator Emil Jones, Jr., Dr. David Slatkin and Dr. Elnora Daniels to realize the founding of the College of Pharmacy, dedicated in 2007, and has proudly served on the Chicago State University Foundation for over a decade; and

WHEREAS, Peggy has made many friends across the political spectrum including President Bill Clinton who appointed her to the White House Women’s Conference, presided over by First Lady Hillary Clinton; Governors James Thompson, Jim Edgar, George Ryan and Pat Quinn who have given her important appointments; and Illinois Secretary of State Jesse White who appointed her to serve on the Illinois Center for the Book; and

WHEREAS, the late Chicago Mayor Harold Washington appointed her to head his first Chicago Commission on Women, and the late Cook County Board President John H. Stroger, Jr. selected her to head his first Cook County Commission on Women’s Issues, created in 1995, with current President Toni Preckwinkle reappointing her in 2016 to continue serving as Commissioner/Chairman for her twenty-fourth year; and

WHEREAS, in 1986 she founded Chicago’s first Celebration of Women’s History Month, commended by Mayor Eugene Sawyer’s 1987 proclamation; in 1988 she co-founded Leadership Illinois; and in 2010 the Cook County Board of Commissioners named the Peggy A. Montes Unsung Heroine Awards in her honor; and
WHEREAS, she was selected for Governor Ryan’s Trade Mission Delegation to South Africa, alongside First Lady Laura Lynn, to explore cultural exchanges between Illinois and South Africa, and for President Barack Obama’s White House Summit on Working Families in 2015; Congressman Bobby Rush appointed her to co-chair the committee that named the 31st Street Margaret T. Burroughs Beach and Park on August 11, 2015; and in 2022, Mayor Lori Lightfoot appointed her to the newly created Black Chicago Heritage Initiative; and

WHEREAS, Peggy recently retired after serving 24 years as Commissioner/Chairman of the Cook County Commission on Women’s Issues, and remains a member of the Illinois Arts Council, the Illinois Book Advisory Committee, the Chicago Art Institute Leadership Advisory Council (founding member), the Griffin Museum of Science and Industry’s Black Creativity Advisory Council, Chicago Links, Inc., Friends of DuSable, DuSable Park Coalition and Advisory Council, Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, and National Sorority of Phi Delta Kappa; she is also a donor and supporter of the Chicago State University Foundation Board and the University of Chicago Medicine Underrepresented in Medicine Visiting Clerkship program; and

WHEREAS, Peggy holds a Bachelor of Arts in Elementary Education from Chicago Teachers College (Chicago State University), awarded June 24, 1960, and a Master of Arts in Counseling and Guidance from Governors State University, awarded December 21, 1974, and was awarded an Honorary Doctorate Degree in Humane Letters from Chicago State University on May 9, 2024; and

WHEREAS, Peggy resides in Chicago, is a widow, and is the proud mother of two - an attorney and an educator - and proud grandmother of three; in her spare time, she collects First Day Covers and unicorns and is a world traveler; and

WHEREAS, Peggy is the recipient of many honors, including the Lifetime Achievement Award from the Association of African American Museums, the Trustee Award from the DuSable Museum, the History Makers Award, the Salute to Excellence Award from Governor George Ryan, the Phenomenal Woman Award from State Farm, the Chicago State University Lifetime Achievement Award, the Woman of Excellence Award from the Chicago Defender, the Legacy Award from the Chicago Commission on Human Relations, and recognition in Who’s Who in Black Chicago; the Cook County Commissioners renamed the annual Women’s Commission Awards the Peggy A. Montes Unsung Heroines Awards in her honor; and

WHEREAS, between 2011 and 2018 she received, among others, the Operation PUSH Keeper of the Village Award, the Cook County Clerk’s Outstanding Woman in Nonprofits Award, the CHURN Living Legacy Award, the Ora Higgins Youth Foundation Distinguished Leadership Award, the WECE Community Dedication Award, the Rainbow PUSH Stand Up For Others Award, and the Chicago State University College of Pharmacy Award for her efforts to establish that college; and

WHEREAS, from 2019 to 2022 her honors included the Mary McLeod Bethune Living Legacy Award, recognition as one of Chicago’s Top Black Women of Impact, the Chicago State University Cougar Servant Leadership Award, dedication of the Peggy A. Montes Playground at the Chicago State University Child Care Center, recognition as a 2021 Notable Non-Profit Board Leader by Crain’s Chicago Business, the DuSable Museum’s Women’s Board Founder’s Award, the Margaret T. Burroughs Legacy Award, and the Mayor Harold Washington Legacy Lifetime Award; and

WHEREAS, from 2023 to 2025 she received the Trailblazer Leadership Award from the Association of African American Museums, the Outstanding Leadership Award from the Association of Children’s Museums, the Stellar Black History Honors Legacy Leadership Award, the Haitian Heritage Association Leadership Award, the Carter G. Woodson Outstanding Leader ASALH Award, and the Outstanding Community Leader Award from the Chicago Cultural Alliance, remaining ever active in cultural and museum advocacy in Chicago; and

WHEREAS, she has been involved for over 36 years in the development of Mayor Harold Washington’s DuSable Park, whose groundbreaking is expected in 2027, and was recently named a 2025 Bud Billiken Parade Honorary Grand Marshal by Chicago Defender Charities and a recipient of Governors State University’s 2025 Distinguished Alumni Award; 

NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the President and Members of the Cook County Board of Commissioners congratulate and honor Dr. Peggy A. Montes on the occasion of her 90th Birthday; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that this Honorable Body extends its deepest gratitude and commendation to Dr. Montes for her many years of exemplary and dedicated service, marked by unwavering commitment, professionalism, and a steadfast dedication to those she has served; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT, this text be spread upon the official proceedings of this Honorable Body and that a suitable copy be presented to Dr. Peggy A. Montes as a symbol of our respect and esteem.

il-17031-bos-matter-81207.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

RESOLUTION HONORING THE LIFE AND LEGACY OF CHARLES ROY “CHUCK” BOWEN SR.       November 23, 1933 - July 31, 2026
WHEREAS, Almighty God, in His infinite wisdom, called from our midst Charles Roy “Chuck” Bowen Sr., a distinguished public servant, political strategist, cultural preservationist, mentor, and steadfast advocate whose extraordinary life and service left an indelible imprint upon Chicago and Cook County; and

WHEREAS, Charles Roy Bowen Sr. was born on November 23, 1933, in Atlanta, Georgia, and moved to Chicago with his mother at the age of eight, where he established a remarkable legacy of civic engagement, political leadership, cultural stewardship, and community empowerment; and

WHEREAS, Mr. Bowen entered public and political life at a young age, distinguishing himself through his extraordinary ability to mobilize communities, cultivate coalitions, and navigate the institutions influencing the political and economic advancement of African Americans in Chicago; and

WHEREAS, throughout his consequential career, Mr. Bowen served as a trusted political liaison, strategist, advisor, and confidant, working alongside prominent leaders including Congressman William L. Dawson and Mayors Richard J. Daley and Richard M. Daley, while building enduring relationships among government, clergy, business leaders, and community institutions; and

WHEREAS, in 1982, Charles Roy Bowen Sr. was elected Cook County Commissioner, where he championed equity and helped advance Cook County’s affirmative action initiatives, expanding contracting opportunities for women and minorities and affirming that economic opportunity should be accessible to every community; and

WHEREAS, following his elected service, Mr. Bowen continued serving Cook County as Deputy Clerk of the Cook County Board, further exemplifying his lifelong commitment to public service and effective government; and

WHEREAS, Mr. Bowen was a devoted guardian of African American history and was instrumental in advocating for the preservation of the historic Eighth Regiment Armory in Bronzeville, helping protect the landmark from demolition and preserve a significant monument to Black military history that today houses the Chicago Military Academy at Bronzeville; and

WHEREAS, Mr. Bowen possessed a profound appreciation for African and African American art and culture, serving as a Co-Founder of the Africa Global Chamber of Commerce and for many years on the Board of Trustees of the International African Festival of the Arts, strengthening cultural and economic connections between Chicago and the African Diaspora; and

WHEREAS, Mr. Bowen generously shared his vast institutional knowledge and firsthand recollections of Chicago’s political and cultural history with younger generations, historians, community leaders, and cultural organizations, with his extraordinary experiences memorialized through the documentary “Citizen Bowen”; and

WHEREAS, affectionately known as “Chuck,” Mr. Bowen was admired for his intellect, wit, generosity, loyalty, political acumen, mentorship, and willingness to open doors for others, embodying a generation of leadership that measured success by communities strengthened, opportunities created, institutions preserved, and lives transformed; and

WHEREAS, the passing of Charles Roy Bowen Sr. on July 31, 2026, represents a profound loss to his family, friends, colleagues, Bronzeville, the African Diaspora, the City of Chicago, and Cook County, while his formidable legacy remains permanently woven into the civic, political, economic, and cultural fabric of the communities he faithfully served; and

NOW, THEREFORE, WE, BILL LOWRY, COOK COUNTY COMMISSIONER OF THE 3rd DISTRICT, AND TONI PRECKWINKLE, PRESIDENT OF THE COOK COUNTY BOARD OF COMMISSIONERS: do hereby honor and commemorate the extraordinary life, distinguished public service, and enduring legacy of CHARLES ROY “CHUCK” BOWEN SR., and extend our most profound condolences to his family, friends, colleagues, mentees, and the countless individuals whose lives were enriched by his leadership and service; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners recognizes Charles Roy Bowen Sr. for his invaluable contributions to Cook County, the City of Chicago, Bronzeville, and the African Diaspora and celebrates a life characterized by civic fortitude, cultural stewardship, political acumen, and an unwavering commitment to the advancement of his community; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that a suitable copy of this Resolution be tendered to the family of Charles Roy “Chuck” Bowen Sr. as an expression of the Cook County Board of Commissioners’ profound respect, gratitude, and enduring appreciation for his exemplary life and consequential legacy. Office of Cook County Commissioner Bill Lowry 3rd.

il-17031-bos-matter-81208.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

RESOLUTION HONORING THE NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF HISPANIC NURSES ILLINOIS CHAPTER ON ITS 40TH ANNIVERSARY

WHEREAS, the National Association of Hispanic Nurses Illinois Chapter, NAHN Illinois, traces its origins to January 1986, when Jesusita Pedroza Sepulveda, RN, brought together a founding committee that recognized the health care needs of Hispanic communities and the impact that the underrepresentation of Hispanic nurses and other health professionals had on access to care; and

WHEREAS, NAHN Illinois is a professional, voluntary, and non-profit health care organization dedicated to enriching the lives of Hispanic nurses through academic attainment, mentorship, professional development, and efforts to improve access to care and reshape health care within Hispanic communities; and

WHEREAS, NAHN Illinois advances Hispanic nurses through education, leadership development, mentorship, professional development, community engagement, and opportunities that strengthen Hispanic representation within the nursing profession; and

WHEREAS, NAHN Illinois elevates the next generation of Hispanic nurses through mentorship programming that supports personal and professional growth through guidance, networking, and professional development opportunities; and

WHEREAS, members of NAHN Illinois gain access to scholarships, mentorship, continuing education, and professional development opportunities to continue their academic and professional advancement; and

WHEREAS, NAHN Illinois serves Hispanic communities throughout Illinois through numerous community outreach initiatives, including health screenings, vaccinations, health education, first aid, and other community health services, while collaborating with organizations committed to serving bilingual, bicultural Spanish speaking communities; and

WHEREAS, the National Association of Hispanic Nurses Illinois Chapter advocates for the health care needs of Hispanic communities at the local, state, and national levels through nursing advocacy, health policy engagement, and opportunities for members to engage with policymakers and other stakeholders; and

WHEREAS, NAHN Illinois supports the future nursing workforce through Pre-Nursing initiatives, mentorship, and community outreach that increase awareness of nursing careers and help strengthen the pipeline of future Hispanic nurses; and

WHEREAS, in 2023, the DAISY Foundation recognized the National Association of Hispanic Nurses Illinois Chapter for its collective efforts and activities to advance health equity and mitigate health disparities; and

WHEREAS, NAHN Illinois has been actively reshaping health care in Hispanic communities for the past 40 years, while advancing Hispanic nurse leadership, improving health outcomes, and advocating for equitable and accessible health care; and

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners hereby recognizes and congratulates the National Association of Hispanic Nurses Illinois Chapter on its 40th anniversary and its significant contributions to nursing, health equity, professional development, mentorship, advocacy, and the health and well-being of Hispanic communities throughout Cook County and Illinois; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that a suitable copy of this resolution be presented to the leadership of the National Association of Hispanic Nurses Illinois Chapter in recognition of 40 years of service, leadership, advocacy, professional development, and commitment to Hispanic nurses and the health and well-being of the communities they serve.

il-17031-bos-matter-81232.title:
PROPOSED ORDINANCE AMENDMENT

AMENDMENT TO INSPECTOR GENERAL ORDINANCE

BE IT ORDAINED, by the Cook County Board of Commissioners, that Chapter 2 Administration, Article IV Officers and Employees, Division 5 Inspector General, Sec. 2-284 and Sec. 2-289 of the Cook County Code is hereby amended as Follows:

Sec. 2-284.  Functions, authority and powers.

In addition to other powers conferred herein, the OIIG shall have the following functions, authority and powers:
(1)	To receive and register complaints and information concerning corruption, fraud, waste, mismanagement, unlawful political discrimination and misconduct in the operations of County Government; including, but not limited to any County contract, grant, lease, license, or application or certification of eligibility for the same; all County employees, departments, bureaus, boards, agencies, agents, or independent contractors; appointed officials, and elected officials in the performance of their official duties; contractors and subcontractors providing goods and services pursuant to a County contract; and all persons and business entities seeking County contracts or certification of eligibility for County contracts.

a.	Complaints and other documents, relating to the Independent Inspector General's investigations of elected officials, shall be verified by certification. The several matters stated in the complaints and other documents shall be stated positively or upon information and belief only, according to the fact. Nothing in this Section shall restrict the Independent Inspector General from exercising his/her independent judgment, based upon an articulable suspicion, to initiate an investigation of an elected official, notwithstanding the existence of any unverified information, or documents, statements and claims submitted anonymously.

b.	The person having knowledge of the matters stated in the complaint or other document certified in accordance with this Section shall subscribe to a certification in substantially the following form: Under penalties as provided by law pursuant to Section 2-291 <https://library.municode.com/il/cook_county/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=PTIGEOR_CH2AD_ARTIVOFEM_DIV5INGE_S2-291VIPE> of the Office of Independent Inspector General Ordinance, the undersigned certifies that the statements set forth in this instrument are true and correct, except as to matters therein stated to be on information and belief and as to such matters the undersigned certifies as aforesaid that he verily believes the same to be true.


c.	Any complaint and other document, relating to the Independent Inspector General's investigations, certified in accordance with this Section may be used in the same manner and with the same force and effect as though subscribed and sworn to under oath.

d.	Any person who intentionally makes a false statement, material to the issue or point in question, in any complaint or other document relating to the Independent Inspector General's investigations of elected officials, and which is certified by such person in accordance with this Section shall be guilty of knowingly furnishing false statements or misleading information and shall be subject to violations and penalties in Section 2-291 <https://library.municode.com/il/cook_county/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=PTIGEOR_CH2AD_ARTIVOFEM_DIV5INGE_S2-291VIPE>.

(2)	To investigate corruption, fraud, waste, mismanagement, unlawful political discrimination and misconduct in operations of County Government under the Offices of the President as well as the separately elected County officials, either in response to such complaints or on the Independent Inspector General's own initiative, or in the proper case, to refer complaints and information to an outside law enforcement agency.

(3)	To promulgate rules and regulations for the conduct of investigations consistent with the requirements of equal protection, due process and this division.

(4)	To request information from and to conduct interviews under oath with County employees, officials, agents, contractors, subcontractors, licensees, grantees or persons or businesses seeking County contracts, grants, licenses, or certification of eligibility for County contracts, for the purpose of investigation of corruption, fraud, waste, mismanagement, unlawful political discrimination, or misconduct. This includes the power to review past, present, and proposed County programs, accounts, records, contracts and transactions.

(5)	To prepare confidential reports and make recommendations for corrective action as outlined in Section 2-285 <https://library.municode.com/il/cook_county/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=PTIGEOR_CH2AD_ARTIVOFEM_DIV5INGE_S2-285CO>.

(6)	To notify the State's Attorney or other appropriate law enforcement authority if the Independent Inspector General determines or suspects that possible criminal conduct has occurred, and to promptly tender to such authorities any evidence or information which has been obtained by the Independent Inspector General. In the event an investigation by the OIIG threatens to interfere with an investigation by a different county, city, state, or federal law enforcement agency, the OIIG will cooperate in all respects with such law enforcement agency. The OIIG shall acquiesce in its investigation only upon written request of another law enforcement agency.

(7)	To notify the Cook County Board of Ethics if the Independent Inspector General determines that a violation of the Cook County Ethics Ordinance has occurred by submitting to the Board of Ethics a copy of the investigation report described in Section 2-288 <https://library.municode.com/il/cook_county/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=PTIGEOR_CH2AD_ARTIVOFEM_DIV5INGE_S2-288COSURE>.

(8)	To serve as liaison between County Government and law enforcement authorities regarding any matters which have been referred to such authorities by the Independent Inspector General.

(9)	To provide quarterly reports to the President and Members of the County Board as outlined in Section 2-287 <https://library.municode.com/il/cook_county/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=PTIGEOR_CH2AD_ARTIVOFEM_DIV5INGE_S2-287QURE>.

(10)	To create and maintain a toll-free "Office of the Independent Inspector General Hotline" for the purpose of receiving reports of corruption, fraud, waste, mismanagement, unlawful political discrimination and misconduct. The identity of any individual placing a call to the Office of the Inspector General Hotline shall be kept confidential during and after the investigation of any complaint made by the caller, unless the caller consents to disclosure of his or her name or disclosure of the caller's identity is otherwise required by law. Alternatively, reports may be made anonymously.

(11)	Notwithstanding any other provision of this Section, the Independent Inspector General shall cooperate with the Shakman Compliance Administrator and fulfill the obligations required in the Supplemental Relief Order entered into by Cook County in Shakman et al. vs. The Democratic Organization of Cook County, et al. No. 69 C 2145 (United States District Court for the Northern District of Illinois), including providing copies of complaints, investigating unlawful political discrimination expeditiously, reporting the results to the Shakman Compliance Administrator, and providing the Shakman Compliance Administrator with quarterly reports.

(12)	The Independent Inspector General shall have, subject to budgetary allocation by the County Board, the sole power to appoint, employ, and remove such assistants, employees and personnel and establish personnel procedures as deemed necessary for the efficient and effective administration of the OIIG.

(13)	To provide a proposed budget request within 90 days of his/her initial appointment and annually thereafter pursuant to the County's fiscal year budget rules and regulations.

(14)	To provide services pursuant to any intergovernmental agreement approved by the Board of Commissioners to which the OIIG is a party.

(15)	To provide services pursuant to a memorandum of understanding to any agency funded by the County Board to which the OIIG is a party and the OIIG determines that a memorandum of understanding is applicable or preferred.

(16)	To participate in and subject its office to peer reviews conducted by the Association of Inspectors General.

Sec. 2-289.  Confidentiality; public statements.

Investigatory files and summary reports concerning alleged corruption, fraud, waste, mismanagement, unlawful political discrimination or misconduct by any person shall be confidential except as provided below or required pursuant to the Supplemental Relief Order entered in the Shakman Case.

(a)	Summary reports shall not be divulged by the Independent Inspector General to any person except to the President, the head of any department or bureau to whose office the investigation pertains, the Chief of the Bureau of Human Resources, accused, Chief Procurement Officer where applicable and to the separately elected official to whose office the investigation pertains. If the investigation involves violations of the Cook County Ethics Ordinance, the Independent Inspector General also shall submit the confidential summary report to the Cook County Board of Ethics.

(b)	Investigatory files shall be confidential, however said files may be divulged with the summary report to the Board of Ethics, the Chief of the Bureau of Human Resources and the head of any department or bureau and elected official to whose office the investigation pertains in order to effectively address matters of discipline or ethical violations. Notwithstanding the foregoing, information or evidence obtained by the Independent Inspector General which pertains to possible criminal activity may be promptly provided to the appropriate law enforcement authorities., and investigatory files may be provided to the Association of Inspectors General during a peer review.

(c)	The Independent Inspector General is authorized to issue public statements concerning:

(1)	An investigation that exonerates an individual who is publicly known to have been under investigation, where the subject requests such a statement.

(2)	An investigation that concerns inefficient or wasteful management, as opposed to individual misconduct or illegality.

(d)	Before issuing a written public statement pursuant Section 2-289 <https://library.municode.com/il/cook_county/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=PTIGEOR_CH2AD_ARTIVOFEM_DIV5INGE_S2-289COPUST>(c)(2) of this Ordinance, involving an OIIG review, inspection, or audit that results in a finding of inefficient or wasteful management the Independent Inspector General must first:

(1)	Share the summary report and written public statement with the head of the department or bureau and elected official to whose office the investigation pertains;

(2)	Allow the head of the department or bureau and elected official to whose office the investigation pertains a period of ten business days in which to provide the Independent Inspector General with a response to the proposed public statement and/or summary report;

(3)	Attach any such response (subject to appropriate redaction) to the Independent Inspector General's public statement and any reply thereto by the Independent Inspector General whenever the Independent Inspector General issues the public statement.

Effective date:  This ordinance shall be in effect immediately upon adoption.

il-17031-bos-matter-81234.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION
